News.title: Charlie Kirk statue vandalized just days after unveiling at Turning Point HQ to mark anniversary of assassination
News.content:
THE newly unveiled Charlie Kirk statue has been vandalized just days after it was installed to mark one year since his assassination.

Kirk, 31, was shot in the neck at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025, just moments after speaking about gun violence as he addressed students.



Thousands witnessed the harrowing shooting as blood was seen gushing from his neck and the dad-of-two fell off his chair in a horrifying act of violence that stunned the nation.

Tyler Robinson, 23, is accused of shooting the Turning Point USA founder from the roof of a nearby campus building.



To honor Kirk on the anniversary of his death, an eight-foot statue was unveiled at Turning Point USA’s headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona, on Thursday.

By Sunday morning it was found vandalized with red spray paint along with a nearby memorial poster, AZFamily reported.

The garish paint is largely concentrated around the neck area where the bullet struck Kirk.

There is also red paint to the face and left hand of the statue and a sad face sprayed onto the stomach.

The Phoenix Police Department confirmed officers were called to Turning Point HQ for “vandalism to a memorial.”

Those with information are urged to contact the department or text 480-WITNESS.



It is not known if police have identified any suspects.

Turning Point USA has not yet responded to a request for comment.

Meanwhile, a $100,000 statue also honoring Kirk was unveiled in Times Square, New York, on Thursday.

There, chaotic scenes quickly erupted as supporters and opponents clashed in the middle of the Big Apple over the divisive figure.

The 6ft 5in bronze-painted sculpture depicts Kirk seated with a microphone and wearing a “FREEDOM” T-shirt.



President Trump honored Kirk at the GOP midterm convention in Dallas on Wednesday night, telling the crowd, “We love you, Charlie,” as his widow Erika received a standing ovation.

Vice President JD Vance also paid tribute to his late friend, while Utah Governor Spencer Cox declared September 10 “Charlie Kirk Day” and called on Americans to reject political violence.

News.title: Brit dad told he ‘MUST return to Cyprus or be arrested’ after son, two, plunged to his death at hotel
News.content:
EXTRADITION THREAT Brit dad told he ‘MUST return to Cyprus or be arrested’ after son, two, plunged to his death at hotel

A BRIT dad accused of “recklessly” causing the death of his toddler in Cyprus has been told he must fly back to the holiday hotspot or face arrest.

The two-year-old boy died at a luxury Cyprus hotel after allegedly slipping from his dad’s arms and falling 33ft to the veranda below.



The father was allowed to return to the UK to attend the tot’s funeral after posting £27,000 bail.

More than 100 mourners attended the service two weeks ago.



But he had been given until September 14 to return to the Mediterranean island.

One well-placed official told The Sun: “If he fails to return to Cyprus, a European arrest warrant will be issued and he will be seized.”

“There is an extradition treaty between Cyprus and the UK and the law is very clear.”

The city exec faces four years in jail if convicted of the charge of causing death “by a rash, reckless or dangerous act” after placing his son on the windowsill before the tragedy occurred on July.

The boy fell through the open pane sustaining severe cranial injuries when he landed 33ft on the veranda below on the first day of the family holiday at the five star King Evelthon hotel in Paphos.

The dad told police he thought the window was closed when he decided to put his son there as he and the boy’s grandfather waited for the lift to arrive.



“That a father who has lost his son is being treated like a criminal is absurd,” a top level judicial source in Cyprus told the Sun.

“The focus from the start should have been on the window and whether, in a hotel corridor leading to the lift, it was right it was open.”

The distraught Brit was arrested at the resort and remanded for eight days in custody before he was charged.

He broke down uncontrollably in court as he appealed for leave to be granted to attend his son’s funeral.

With a trial set for Thursday in Paphos, the Essex-born man made a dramatic plea last week to the island’s Attorney General, George Savvides, to have the criminal charges dropped on humanitarian grounds.



The Brit’s Nicosia-based lawyer Alexandros Alexandou said: “We have asked the Attorney General to discontinue this prosecution on public interest and humanitarian grounds.

“In these exceptional circumstances, we do not believe a continued criminal process serves the public interest.

“The family has already suffered an unimaginable loss, and the focus now should be on their welfare and recovery’.”

As the former Brit colony’s top legal authority, it lies “completely within the discretion” of Savvides to drop the case or ensure it goes ahead.

Once made, his decision cannot be overturned.



“Everything rests on his decision,” said the source. “This is a tragedy from beginning to end.”

News.title: Shocking moment two motorcyclists perform dangerous stunt in middle of busy highway and get instant karma
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment two motorcyclists perform a dangerous stunt on a busy highway before instantly paying the price.

Idaho State Police shared dash cam footage from a crash on the I-84 in Boise in which the pair of riders performed wheelies on the busy highway.



One rider dressed all in black is seen rearing his motorbike onto the back wheel while driving down the lane lines surrounded by other vehicles.

The car where the dash cam footage came from then moves into the inner lane, revealing a second motorcyclist performing the same dangerous trick just a moment later.



However, the rider quickly loses control and is tipped off balance after raising the bike onto one wheel.

In a horrifying moment, the rider is seen going backwards as the bike flips, coming off the seat and hitting the highway as sparks fly from the impact of both him and the bike scraping the road.

Before the footage cuts out the rest of the impact, a car was seen following closely behind but it seems that they were able to avoid colliding with the rider.

News.title: Teenage boy, 16, dies after car crashes into tree injuring two others as driver, 18, arrested
News.content:
CRASH PROBE Teenage boy, 16, dies after car crashes into tree injuring two others as driver, 18, arrested

A TEENAGE boy has died after the car he was in smashed into a tree, as the cops arrest one man.

The 16-year-old was a passenger in a blue Volkswagen Polo, which was travelling along the A4104 in Worcestershire on Saturday night, September 12.

The vehicle was heading towards Dunstall when it collided with a tree between the carriageway and the slip road to Bourne Road at around 9.20pm.



The teenage boy suffered “significant injuries” and was pronounced dead at the scene, according to West Mercia Police.



Two other passengers, also teens aged 16 and 17, suffered minor injuries.

Police have arrested an 18-year-old man on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and driving in excess of drink and drugs.

He has been interviewed and since bailed as police enquiries continue.



The force has appealed for any witnesses to the collision to come forward.

Detective Sergeant Rose Hughes from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit said: “Firstly, our thoughts are with the family and loved ones of the boy who tragically lost his life yesterday.

“They are being supported by specialist officers and will be kept informed throughout the investigation process.

“We are now appealing for witnesses who may have seen the collision, or the vehicle travelling prior to the incident taking place.



“If you have any information or dashcam footage which may help us piece together the moments leading up to the collision, please get in contact with us.”

Information can be passed on to the force via email at sciusouth@westmercia.police.uk or by calling 101.

News.title: Fury grows as MPs demand US ‘paedo’ diplomat is extradited back to UK after Yanks’ ‘grotesque’ dawn raid
News.content:
EMBASSY ROW Fury grows as MPs demand US ‘paedo’ diplomat is extradited back to UK after Yanks’ ‘grotesque’ dawn raid

BRITISH cops and ministers must demand the return of a suspected paedophile secretly flown to the US after “high-handed” Americans dodged international law to remove him, say experts.

They spoke out after we told how a US snatch squad raided the diplomat’s London home without telling the Met Police and bundled him onto a cargo flight to Dover Air Force base, Delaware.



Politicians, lawyers and ex-cops have voiced their anger at the move – revealed in the Sun on Sunday – as they demanded officials stand up to the Yanks.

Tory MP Ben Obese-Jecty called the cloak and dagger US move “absolutely grotesque”.



He added: “The US government is now protecting alleged paedophiles.

“US Marines conducting a raid on British soil, on which they have no jurisdiction, to seize one of their own diplomats and use US military resources to ferry the suspect out of the country is completely unacceptable.”



And lawyer Mark Stephens – an expert in international litigation who has represented Julian Assange – said: “The Americans have shown a heavy-handed disregard for our law and effectively extraordinarily rendered one of their own citizens.

“It is embarrassing and it seems astonishing that they have done this without alerting the Metropolitan Police.



“They have ignored international law.

“Most right-thinking people would be sick to their stomach as there are issues of public confidence and reassurance at play here.

“If a crime is committed here the crime should be tried here, and there are potentially victims of abuse in this country.

“But there is nothing to stop the Metropolitan Police from presenting evidence and charging this individual, and demanding his extradition.

“In this case I believe that is the path they must follow.”



And Rebecca Niblock, a specialist extradition lawyer at Kingsley Napley, said: “As a matter of international law, one state cannot ordinarily exercise its law enforcement powers in the territory of another state without its consent.

“To do so may infringe that state’s sovereignty and raises both legal and diplomatic issues.”

US officials searched the diplomat’s home in Putney, London on August 25 after discovering his brother in Illinois was allegedly sending him child abuse images.

They are said to have discovered further abuse material after raiding the address and then whisked the man – who worked at the US embassy in Nine Elms, south London – to RAF Fairford, Gloucs where there is a large American presence.

A Boeing then flew to Delaware and then on to O’Hare Airport in Chicago, Illinois, 4,000 miles from London.



Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley has hosted crisis meetings about the case while No10 and the Foreign Office are being kept updated.

Ministers are set to hold crunch talks this week as they prepare a response to America, while Andy Burnham is due to meet Donald Trump in New York in just over a week.

The case has echoes of the case of Harry Dunn, 19, who was killed in a 2019 crash on the wrong side of the road by US citizen Anne Sacoolas who fled and never returned to the UK.

Ex Met Police Detective Mick Neville said: “The Americans should not have done this, and it’s a very embarrassing situation.

“We should make an official request for his extradition but they are likely to just say no.



“Sadly we are very limited in what we can do and once he was on that plane it was likely game over.

“If we couldn’t get Anne Sacoolas back after the death of Harry Dunn we probably won’t get this bloke back.”

A Met Police spokesperson said: “On Tuesday, 25 August, US authorities made us aware of an investigation they are conducting into suspected offences in London relating to indecent images of children.

“We continue to liaise with them regarding this matter.”

The US Embassy has confirmed the probe and said it will “continue to work closely with law enforcement partners regarding these allegations.”

News.title: Huge wildfire erupts in Brit holiday hotspot Costa del Sol with residents evacuated & emergency alert issued
News.content:
A MASSIVE wildfire has broken out in a Costa del Sol village with residents forced to evacuate amid an emergency alert.

At least five helicopters and over 60 firefighters raced to the inferno in Benahavis, near Brit tourist hotspot Marbella, and are furiously battling the flames.



The raging blaze is believed to have been sparked inside a small Catholic chapel at around 3pm.

Dramatic photos show fiery red flames scorching treetops as a monstrous wall of thick smoke billows across the region.



The wildfire ripped through the hillsides close to the mountain village as shocked residents watched on.

Emergency text messages have pinged across the region as anxious locals strive to escape unharmed from the fires.



Residents have been urged to hunker down in their homes and shut all doors and windows as choking smoke spirals through the air.

The number of planes and helicopters involved has risen to around 20.

Andalucia’s Acting Minister for Health said: “If you are in the area, shelter inside a masonry house or building.

“Close doors and windows. Follow the instructions from 1-1-2 and the emergency services. Avoid risks.”



One stricken eyewitness said that the village of Benahavis was in a “terrible state”.

She told Spanish newspaper The Olive Press: “We managed to get out. They aren’t letting anyone in anymore.

“The vegetation along the entire road leading to the village is on fire. It’s horrible.”



Firefighting efforts have been hampered by strong winds gusting up to 30mph, according to witnesses speaking to the paper.

Meanwhile, a luxury residential estate near the spot where the wildfire started was evacuated this evening.

The gated area of Montemayor Alto is home to around 125 upmarket villas.

A regional government-run emergency response co-ordination centre confirmed the evacuation just after 6.30pm local time.

It comes just months after deadly wildfires devastated the hillsides of Almeria, killing 15.



Nine Brits were among the victims of the horrifying blaze on July 9.

Just days ago one Brit woman died in hospital two months after getting trapped in the devastating Spanish wildfires.

Expat Michelle Leake suffered horror burns across her body and was being treated in an intensive care unit at Seville’s Virgen del Rocio University Hospital before she succumbed to her injuries.

Mum-of-three Lisa Fryett, another victim of the Bedar wildfire, died in the same Seville hospital on July 28.

The 47-year-old, from Canvey Island, Essex, was staying near the village with her partner Simon Batchelor, who was also airlifted critically injured to the hospital’s specialist burns unit after being rescued by police.



A 93-year-old British woman who has not been formally named died in hospital three days after the first 12 people were killed the day the wildfire started.

Expat couple Pete and Fran Gillam were also among those killed in the wildfires.

Sheffield-based daughter Danielle Gillam-Kirton has since claimed police have botched the investigation into their deaths.

A further four Brits tragically entered a “death trap” as they desperately tried to escape the raging flames.

HAYDEN Panettiere’s on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson was cuffed by cops last night after an alleged incident at a bar.

According to sources, the 37-year-old actor started yelling at officers about her death while cuffed and sitting on the sidewalk.



Brian had allegedly been drinking for hours with his brother Zach at the Wild Wing Cafe bar in Greenville, South Carolina, on Saturday night before the pair were thrown out over a chair tossing incident, TMZ reports.

Sources told the outlet that the outing took a turn when Brian went up to the bar to talk to fellow patrons before allegedly picking up a stool and throwing it behind him.



Video obtained by TMZ shows Brian being raised into the air by someone during an argument before being carried out of the bar while a bartender yells “Let him go!”

The Greenville Police Department told the outlet that they were called to the bar about an alleged assault and found the two brothers in an argument with others outside.

Both men were put in cuffs but only Zach was arrested for disorderly conduct after launching into a profanity-filled tirade.

Brian was released by cops but not before accusing the police department of leaking information about Hayden’s death.

“GPD leaked it when my girlfriend died,” he yelled after officers put him in cuffs, per TMZ.

Last month, the Heroes and Nashville star was found unresponsive at her Greenville apartment where she had been staying with Brian.

Hayden’s exact cause of death remains unknown

Meanwhile, a criminal investigation has reportedly been launched to find out if anyone was responsible for her death.

Following Hayden’s tragic death, her mother Lesley Vogel slammed her daughter’s rekindled relationship with Brian, revealing that the family were desperate to “get rid” of him.

The pair began dating in 2018 and the following year after the family already raised concerns about the relationship, Brian was arrested for domestic violence after an incident at Hayden’s home.



The actress allegedly sustained injuries to her arms, ears, and neck area.

But just a few days after his arrest, they were spotted holding hands while shopping for new cars despite him being hit with a felony charge which was later dismissed in part due to no cooperating witnesses.

On Valentine’s Day 2020, Brian was arrested again for domestic violence while the pair was vacationing in Wyoming and he was sentenced to 45 days in jail. According to reports, he served 12 days in jail.



Despite Hayden releasing a statement about the abusive nature of the relationship, the pair were seen together again in July 2021, shortly before Brian was accused of getting into a massive group brawl in Hollywood.

News.title: Moment Ukraine naval drone ‘destroys unmanned Russian boat’ in ‘first-ever’ drone battle at sea
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment Ukraine destroys a Russian boat in the “first ever” battle between sea drones.

Multiple rounds of machine-gun fire blast into the hull of the unmanned Russian drone in newly released footage fromUkraine‘s navy.



After a volley of strikes, the bot submerges beneath the waves in a huge shower of water and thick, grey smoke.

Writing on Telegram yesterday, the Ukrainian navy called the mid-sea clash the “first-ever” battle between sea drones.



“This marks the first-ever naval engagement between uncrewed surface vessels”, the statement said.

Filmed aboard a Ukrainian Sargan 3000 USV vessel, the footage shows an M2 Browning .50 machine gun take aim.



It then fires across the sea, striking and sinking Putin’s sea drone as empty cartridges tumble from the weapon.

Bristling with heavy machine guns, unmanned sea bots can destroy vessels at distances of 2,000 yards and fire between 450–575 rounds per minute.

Intelligence gathered by Ukraine’s Main Intelligence Directorate detetcted the Russian target – and then fed the information back to the unmanned vessel

It is unclear precisely when the dramatic sea clash took place.



Deadly drone swarms unleashed by Ukraine have pushed back Vladimir Putin‘s armies – and are changing the scarred face of warfare forever.

Just days ago Ukraine hammered Siberian gas plants – which are 2,000 miles from the border – in its deepest strike into Russia to date.

The relentless attacks on fuel hubs is shattering Russia’s economy – and has left furious citizens brawling over petrol.



Volodymr Zelensky has spurred his forces into buidling some of the world’s most high-tech drones – with the latest invention dubbed “The Sun”.

The deadly new drone is creating a vast “kill zone” across the front line – pushing the battlefield towards a stalemate.

It can fly up to 190mph – and boasts an almost 100 per cent kill rate.

And in August, British-made drones struck Russia for the first time, killing at least six people in the biggest air raid on Moscow in two years.

More than 800 flying bots swarmed through the skies and rained hell down on Russia warehouses and factories.



Drone warfare has become a defining feature of the Ukraine-Russia war.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They are everywhere and do everything, from sinking ships to hauling half-dead soldiers off the battlefield.

Experts believe they are the new “kings of war” with defence ministries across the world pouring more cash into developing the deadly bots.

News.title: Women ditch health fads after ‘quick-fix’ diets leave them disappointed
News.content:
Women ditch health fads after ‘quick-fix’ diets leave them disappointed

More than half of women have given up on extreme health fads after being left feeling misled by quick-fix diets and celebrity fitness videos.

Vitabiotics Wellwoman ask the public about health fads

The cabbage soup diet, juice cleanses and celebrity home workouts have been identified amongst the most significant health fads that women are relieved to leave behind.

‌



Research involving 2,000 women revealed numerous once-trendy dietary approaches - including the baby food diet, grapefruit diet and Atkins diet - that women no longer consider worthwhile. Exercise trends such as Insanity workouts, hot yoga, and the Nintendo Wii Fit have similarly lost their appeal.

‌



Following decades of wellness crazes, 43% of women are now more sceptical about health fads than previously, primarily because they've discovered there are no quick wins.

‌



Women are now more likely to concentrate on straightforward sustainable strategies such as increasing their water intake or walking more.

Eating more fruit and vegetables, exercising more regularly or taking vitamins and supplements were also among the things women would now rather do.

View 3 Images Women are choosing consistent healthy habits over diet fads (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Melissa Cohen, head of nutrition at Vitabiotics Wellwoman , which commissioned the research, said: "Some of these health fads were staples in years gone by. But times have changed and women are now looking at a more holistic approach to wellness and building consistent healthy habits.

"We've all had the disappointment of trying something that seemed like a quick fix, and often it is the simpler approaches that see the best results.

"Simply improving your diet and nutrition, being more active and ensuring you get enough sleep can be all it takes to notice a difference in how you feel."

‌



View 3 Images These include regular exercise and balanced eating (Image: Getty Images)

Over half of women (51%) have experimented with a wellness and fitness fad or trend, with intermittent fasting (29%), the Slim Fast diet (26%) and step aerobics (23%) proving the most popular choices.

Zumba (23%), celebrity fitness DVDs and videos (22%) and even the Nintendo Wii Fit (21%) have also attracted a strong following. Yet many were left feeling let down, with 21% feeling misled and 20% annoyed.

‌



Two thirds cannot imagine trying a health and fitness fad now, with 47% of those being more concerned about their overall health and wellbeing than chasing a quick-fix trend.

Four in ten are now more committed to making consistent lifestyle changes (40%) or prefer to stick to more tried-and-tested methods (30%).

View 3 Images Building better habits will help improve wellbeing long term (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The study, conducted through OnePoll, revealed that 62% consider their health and wellbeing 'very important', with two thirds also stating it is more of a priority for them than it was ten years ago.

However, as lives become increasingly hectic, 62% are seeking a more straightforward approach to health and wellness, with 50% admitting it is often the first thing to be neglected when time is short.

Melissa Cohen, from Vitabiotics Wellwoman, added: "Women's lives are getting busier, and it's often our health and wellbeing that can drop off when things feel a bit fraught.

"Making it as simple as possible is key for you to be able to continue being consistent with your health and wellness goals."

News.title: Woman arrested after man injured in 'chemical substance' incident
News.content:
Woman arrested after man injured in 'chemical substance' incident

A 40-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm after a man was hospitalised in a "chemical substance" incident in Crawley

View Image The incident happened at an address in Southgate, Crawley

A woman has been arrested after a man was rushed to hospital in Crawley with injuries from a "chemical substance" incident.

Emergency services rushed to a property in Fletcher Close, Southgate, at around 5.10am this morning where a 40-year-old man was treated at the scene and taken to hospital.

A woman, also aged 40, was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and police said she was taken to hospital as a precaution.

A police cordon was put in place on Fletcher Close while emergency services remained at the scene as part of an investigation.

In a statement from Sussex Police, the force said that there is not thought to be a wider threat to the public following the incident involving a chemical substance.

No further details have been given so far from police about what type of chemical substance was involved or how serious are the injuries to the man.

A spokesperson for Sussex Police said: “Emergency services responded to an incident involving a chemical substance which took place at an address in Fletcher Close, Southgate, Crawley on Sunday 13 September at around 5.10am.

“There is no wider risk to the public.

“A 40-year-old man has been taken to hospital to be treated for injuries, and a 40-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm. She has been taken to hospital as a precaution.

“A temporary road closure was in place in Fletcher Close while emergency services remained at the scene.”

It comes after the couple's former neighbour claimed the pair neglected to tell their children’s school that they were starting a new life in the UK and left the United States in such a hurry they even left their pet fish behind.

Their return has already suffered a set-back. Uganda's decision to withdraw from Prince Harry's Invictus Games is a 'consequence' of the King's cutting letter on the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's royal status, it has been claimed.

Buckingham Palace issued the 'guidance' on the monarch's behalf on Monday, declaring in no uncertain terms that the couple have not returned to the UK as working royals.

‌



View 5 Images The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have waved goodbye to California (Image: AP)

Interior designer Penny Bianchi claimed that Harry and Meghan, still waiting to hear whether they will be given taxpayer-funded security, kept the school in the dark over the return to the UK.

“The school hated their bodyguards," she said in an interview with The Sun. "They would drop the children off with them. To be honest, nobody really liked them here very much. They aren’t popular.”

‌



She went on: “My grandchildren go to the same school as my son, so I get all my gossip from there. Archie goes to the school and they didn’t even know they were leaving until everyone else found out."

Ms Bianchi claimed the move had been spoken about for a long while but as soon as Archie was accepted in a UK school, "they practically left the next day".

Article continues below

Team Sussex sources said security reasons were behind the hush-hush exit, with bodyguards on the school run not unusual in California. Residents have told how they are "worried" they are for the koi carp, which “need to be looked after 24/7”.

The King issued a letter to "senior stakeholders" on Monday where he has made it clear that - despite being back in the UK - his son and Meghan should be considered "private citizens".

In a firm letter statement on his behalf, it stated that the Sussexes' should not use their HRH styles, which are still in abeyance, and that they "do not represent the sovereign" while out making public appearances.

News.title: Woman says she's 'tired' trying to prove she's alive after being declared dead by government
News.content:
Woman says she's 'tired' trying to prove she's alive after being declared dead by government

The elderly Florida widow says the mistake has repeatedly caused problems with her finances and official records, despite being told the error had already been corrected

View 2 Images The 84-year-old was told her Social Security number belonged to someone who had died (Image: WFLA News Channel 8/Youtube)

An 84-year-old woman has spent more than two years trying to prove to government agencies that she is still alive after being mistakenly declared dead.

‌



Priscilla Slack says the bizarre mix-up began after her husband died two years ago, when she was somehow also listed as deceased. The mistake seemed like a small administrative error which would quickly be resolved but two years on it has affected vital parts of her life.

‌



Her bank account was first to be affected. Priscilla said : “First they cancelled my bank account, and they cancelled my credit card. When I went to vote, I was still cancelled."

‌



View 2 Images Priscilla has been passed between government agencies for years (Image: WFLA News Channel 8/Youtube)

She initially tried to see the funny side, assuming the mistake would be quickly put right. She told NBC affiliate WFLA: “I kept my sense of humour about it early on, because we can all make mistakes and push the wrong button”

But the mix-up was not resolved as the problems continued to grow. Priscilla said the original error came from the Social Security Administration, and although she believed it had been corrected, other agencies continued to act as though she was dead.

‌



Each time she thought the issue had finally been resolved, another problem appeared. She has since faced many difficulties including holding bank accounts, paying taxes and voting, with agencies periodically requiring her to prove again that she is alive.

Most recently, Priscilla received a letter from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) claiming she had filed a tax return using the Social Security number of someone who was deceased forcing her to prove that the number belonged to her.

Priscilla said attempts to resolve the problem have involved being repeatedly passed between the IRS and the Social Security Administration. She said: “How am I supposed to deal with these agencies who can’t deal with each other?”

Article continues below

Priscilla believes the agencies involved should now be responsible for correcting the records rather than leaving her to keep challenging the mistake.

The problems have continued for more than two years since her husband’s death, despite Priscilla previously being told the Social Security error had been corrected. She says other agencies have continued to flag her records and freeze accounts when the incorrect information resurfaces.

A spokesperson for the IRS said the matter was being escalated to an advocacy department in an effort to resolve it, according to WFLA.

News.title: Major EES update for 9 UK tourist hotspots including Portugal
News.content:
Major EES update for 9 UK tourist hotspots including Portugal

The European Union entry-exit system (EES) has caused repeated delays for Brits at major EU airports this year

View 3 Images (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

British holidaymakers heading abroad may finally be able to breathe a sigh of relief over the widely-criticised EES system. The scheme forces non-EU residents to queue at special machines in airports before gaining entry to 29 nations within the so-called Schengen area – essentially the majority of the European Union.

‌



However, there have been persistent reports of lengthy delays – some stretching to as long as four hours. A new report in the Sunday Times now reveals that the European Union has shelved the controversial entry-exit system (EES) across at least nine countries.

‌



Portugal, Italy, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Malta, Greece and Switzerland are all understood to have been granted permission to postpone full implementation of EES. The newspaper reports that there appears to be no deadline by which these countries must adopt the scheme, which has already sparked widespread reports of enormous queues at European airports this summer in destinations such as Mallorca, Faro, the Canary Islands and Milan.

‌



The scheme has faced fierce criticism from Ryanair and others. The European Union describes the Entry/Exit System (EES) as an automated IT system designed to register non-EU nationals travelling on short stays each time they cross the external borders of participating European countries.

Following years of postponements, the system was rolled out from October 2025, with full implementation originally anticipated by the following April. However, faced with the prospect of significant border queues due to software failures, officials granted countries a 150-day grace period during which they could drop the checks to avoid travel chaos.

That rule ended on September 6. The EU previously insisted there would be no extension.

‌



View 3 Images (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

Yet the Sunday Times reports that at least nine Schengen countries are understood to have told the European Commission, which is responsible for overseeing the EES, that they would not enforce the new controls in full until the technology and systems were working correctly.

They have informally been allowed to do so with no time limits apparently in place to adopt the system, it is being reported. One of the main purposes of the system is to track whether non-EU citizens have spent more than their permitted 90 days in the bloc in a rolling 180-day period.

‌



Social media has been awash with debate about the scheme. One post on Reddit saw a traveller say: "They made a mess of it. Seems many basic things like it is hit and miss on the document scanning but also things like people walk up with hats and headphones and the machine doesn't tell them to remove them, and organisational things like if the machine errors the traveller has to back out and has no where to go.

"The right way to do this would have been progressive: start by getting some people eg 5% going through the machine lane, everyone else through normal.

"The vendor observes problems, fixes them, once machine working well, increase to 10%, then 20% and so on." Another person said: "The general lack of functionality of so many IT systems across the EU is kind of astonishing."

‌



A third added: "It's worse than that. There isn't even consistent protocol/IT support within a single EU airport."

Another put it more simply, saying: "I just miss having stamps."

'People are missing their flights'

Nadia, from Greater Manchester, told the Guardian in August she had made two trips to Schengen areas this summer. A trip to Tenerife in June was "quite straightforward", but her experience in July at Frankfurt airport where she was picking up a connecting flight home, was much less so.

‌



"The queue there was ridiculously long, and there was very limited information," she says. "People were wandering around trying to work out where they needed to go.

View 3 Images The new entry and exit system (EES) has led to huge delays for passengers, with some missing flights (Image: Getty)

"I'm very well travelled and pretty confident, but even I was slightly unsure and was thinking, is there some other queue I should be joining? There was no one nearby to check with without losing your place."

Article continues below

Eventually, her passport was checked. "He didn't actually take fingerprints then," says Nadia, who is a solicitor. "I think the queue was so long they decided to dispense with that.

"It's the efficiency of the system I question and the fact that individual member states' systems do not talk to one another. They shouldn't need to get information again if you have already gone through. It's pretty shambolic, and I think people missing their flights because of it is just not acceptable, especially when there's no recourse; it's not your fault."

Ryanair chief executive Michael O'Leary has repeatedly complained about EES. Speaking earlier this year, he said: "There's a bit of Brexit in this too. Here, you voted for Brexit - f***ing join the queue."

News.title: King Charles to urge AI chiefs to use the technology 'for good of humanity'
News.content:
King Charles to urge AI chiefs to use the technology 'for good of humanity'

Charles is due to host a summit with the leaders major AI companies where he will encourage them to reach a consensus on a “shared set of principles”

View 4 Images King Charles will host a summit of AI chiefs (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

King Charles will this week ask leaders of the world’s most powerful AI firms to use the technology “for the good of humanity”.

‌



Charles is due to host a summit with the leaders from Anthropic, Nvidia, Google DeepMind and Open AI at Dumfries House, Scotland, where he will encourage them to reach a consensus on a “shared set of principles”.

‌



The importance of his plea was underlined when the boss of the AI giant Anthropic called for development of the technology to be slowed.

‌



View 4 Images Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham taking part in Great North Run to raise funds for homeless charity READ MORE :

Angela Rayner hits back at Donald Trump over united Ireland outburst READ MORE :

In an open letter, Dario Amodei said AI had been “advancing drastically faster” since the summer and could be capable of taking over the “entire internet” and “potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage” in the next six to 12 months.

‌



Amodei, who co-founded Anthropic with his sister Daniela in 2021, said: “Left unchecked, it could outrun our ability to understand and control these systems, and so must be pursued very carefully, if at all.”

Charles, 77, who has never owned a mobile phone, is understood to have taken a keen interest in AI’s development and the risks it posed.

View 4 Images Charles will host AI bosses at Dumfries House (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A source said he hopes the summit would encourage tech leaders to consider “the responsibilities of developing this technology, as well as the opportunities”.

It is understood delegates at the summit will include Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and chief executive; Sir Demis Hassabis, the founder and chairman of Google DeepMind; Niccolo de Masi, the chair and chief executive of IonQ; and Paolo Benanti, an adviser to the Vatican on AI.

A royal source told the Sunday Times: “The King is there to convene, listen and encourage those discussions and to pose the question of: ‘How do we develop AI for the good of humanity?’

‌



“As we've seen him do on issues like the environment and water scarcity, he is hoping to provide a neutral space to aid conversations that are part of a national and global issue on something that is going to impact all of us.

“He hopes the discussions bring about a wider understanding of the responsibilities of developing this technology, as well as the opportunities, ensuring any technological development remains centred around human benefit for communities.

“He wants to ask the question: ‘Would it be helpful to have a set of principles?’ His feeling is it is not an easy thing to do, but that doesn't mean we shouldn't try.”

‌



View 4 Images King Charles and Queen Camilla (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Charles's opening remarks are expected to “encourage collaborative, open discussion from all, and pose the question of whether guiding principles could help positive progress in this pace, on a topic that will in some way impact us all”.

The King's aides have consulted the government on the summit, which will be attended by Kanishka Narayan, the AI minister.

‌



The event at Dumfries House, which is headquarters of The King's Foundation, will be overseen by the Ditchley Foundation, which has drawn up the draft charter for AI leaders.

The charter is understood to include a "shared set of principles" that, if agreed, would "help guide the future application of AI, not merely as a driver of capability and efficiency, but as a tool that upholds human dignity and contributes to the flourishing of both people and the planet".

Charles has also asked for "side discussions" to take place between AI leaders and representatives from his charities including The King's Trust, formerly The Prince's Trust, the Sustainable Markets Initiative and The King's Foundation, to explore the impact AI will have on young people, business, the environment and the developing world.

‌



Last year, Charles awarded the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering to Huang, the founder of Nvidia ? the world's most valuable company with a market cap of $5.29 trillion (£3.9 trillion) ? alongside six other AI pioneers.

Last week, AI experts aired their fears that the technology was advancing so rapidly, it could “kill all humans” within the next decade.

Evan Hubinger, a senior safety researcher at Anthropic, said on X: “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade.”

‌



On Thursday, Anthropic, one of the world's largest AI companies valued at nearly £1 trillion revealed that it had caught external researchers trying to use its technology to model harmful viruses that could be used as potential biological weapons.

Hubinger's remarks were in response to another post on X from Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher who resigned from Anthropic on Tuesday, and had worked at OpenAI.

He posted: “Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to selfimproving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.

‌



"Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources.”

Coxon told the BBC: “I believe that if we don't slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future.”

Shadow Foreign Secretary Tom Tugendhat said government “does not have the speed to keep up with” AI advances and “we need to maintain that ability to protect ourselves”.

‌



He told Sky News: “It does sometimes feel like you're watching somebody loading a machine gun and then warning you that the machine gun's dangerous.

“The reality is there are real dangers with AI and controls on things like bio-weapons or on the development of new forms of nuclear threat are things that the AI services are aware of.

“But we saw recently with the Hugging Face attack the various different ways in which breakout capabilities have been enabled.”

Article continues below

Mr Tugendhat added: “The speed of change is also extraordinary, and this is where actually government can enable a conversation, but we simply do not have the speed to keep up with the advances that are happening.

“And the reality is, we can't pass laws against mathematics. These are mathematical equations that are being developed in greater and greater speed, and we need to maintain that ability to protect ourselves.”

News.title: Reform confident it won't need to repay any of £72m under proposed new donor rules
News.content:
Reform UK believes the Â£72m in donations it has received from two cryptocurrency billionaires were "entirely in line with the law", the party's economic spokesman has said.

Robert Jenrick told the BBC he did not expect that the party will have to return any of the money from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, who are both British and have spent time living overseas.

The government is seeking to change the law on donations to UK political parties from British expats, including a Â£100,000 cap backdated to 25 March.

"These two donations are entirely in line with the law as it is and, as far as we know, the law as it's going to be in the future," Jenrick said.

As well as limiting how much British citizens can donate to political parties from overseas, the government has proposed a minimum residency period in which the Â£100,000 cap would still apply for those who move back to the UK.

This would be in place for the remainder of the calendar year and the following calendar year after the person returns.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that the rule changes would apply retrospectively and anyone not complying with them would have "to return that money".

Rayner added she was not commenting specifically on Delo and Harborne as she does not "understand" their "circumstances".

Answering questions about the donations following Rayner's remarks, Jenrick said: "It might be that Angela Rayner or the government keep trying to change the law to make it even harder for people to donate to Reform, nothing would surprise me.

"But, as it stands, we believe these are entirely in line with the law."

BBC News has been told that both Delo and Harborne have returned to the UK. Delo is understood to have been back in the country since last year.

Jenrick said Delo had returned to the UK "in part so that he can comply with the changes to the law".

In a statement after the programme, a Reform UK spokesman said: "We are 100% confident both [donations] are legal and won't ever have to handed back."

One person familiar with the government's proposed changes said the issue of whether Delo and Harborne are affected would likely come down to how ministers choose to define UK residency.

They said one way would be to adopt the same definition used in tax laws, but stressed how complex the rules around residency are.

News.title: Andy Burnham among Great North Run finishers
News.content:
The Great North Run (GNR) returned to Tyneside this weekend, with 63,000 runners taking part in the world's biggest half marathon - including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

England star and Newcastle captain Dan Burn rang the starter's bell, with famous faces including football personality Chris Kamara and fitness coach Joe Wicks taking on the challenge.

The 13.1-mile (21km) event saw runners and wheelchair users race from Newcastle through Gateshead and South Tyneside, before finishing in South Shields.

Britons David Weir and Melanie Woods won the men's and women's elite wheelchair races respectively. Brigid Kosgei won the elite women's contest and Zouhair Talbi won the men's race.

The half marathon is in its 45th year and raises about Â£25m for charity each time.

News.title: 'Slim chance' government will hit 1.5m new homes target, Rayner tells BBC
News.content:
There is only a "slim chance" the government will meet its target of building 1.5 million homes in England by the next election, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has told the BBC.

"Headwinds" including the Iran war and rising construction costs are making it harder to meet the key Labour manifesto pledge, Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg.

"But I'm definitely not giving it up," she said, and stressed that the government was "making a difference" through investing billions in social and affordable homes.

Data up to June this year suggested the government was behind on the rate of construction needed to meet the goal, which housebuilders have previously warned was too optimistic.

Labour promised to hit the target through building both private and social housing by the end of the current parliament, meaning summer 2029 at the latest.

This implied an average of 300,000 new properties would be needed each year - a rate of construction not seen in decades.

Rayner told the BBC on Sunday: "It's a slim chance, but I'm definitely not giving it up."

She said it was important to keep the goal - which she said had always been a "stretch target" - in place, but that she was "being honest with the public" that it would be difficult to achieve.

News.title: Meghan shares glimpse of family life after Sussexes return to UK
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has shared a glimpse of family life in footage posted to Instagram following their return to the UK.

The 34-second clip, which features Wham!'s Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go, begins with Meghan, along with her husband Prince Harry, walking along a country path as she turns and says "come on, you".

UK flag and heart emojis are shown throughout the video, which also shows their son Archie running towards deer as their daughter Lilibet rides her bike.

Another clip sees Harry fishing with the children as their dog walks alongside the water.

It's the first time the Duchess has posted her family on her Instagram grid since the Sussexes returned from from the US after living in California.

It is unclear when, or where, the footage posted on Sunday afternoon was taken, external, but one clip shows a pair of wellington boots walking on the spot in a puddle and the children also appear to be in waterproof boots as they head toward the deer.

The UK has had a wet start to September after experiencing its hottest summer on record.

The post offers a rare glimpse into the lives of seven-year-old Archie and five-year-old Lilibet.

Whereas Meghan does occasionally show the couple's children on social media, their faces are often obscured as they are photgraphed from behind or their faces are hidden by their parents.

Alongside all the outside footage, there is also a moment showing a child's feet in front of an open fire.

News.title: Police searching for six men over anti-migrant protest in Portsmouth
News.content:
The government condemned "intimidating and thuggish behaviour" at the demonstration, while stressing the right to peaceful protest.

On Friday, a 42-year-old man from Paulsgrove was charged with violent disorder and assaulting a police officer in connection with the incident. He has been remanded into custody.

A 16-year-old boy was arrested on Saturday in connection with the disorder. He has been released on bail pending further enquiries.

Rowlinson said: "The reality of public order policing is that arrests at the time are not always possible, especially where evidence may need to be reviewed to clearly identify who is responsible for offences."

The force had reviewed "hundreds of hours' worth" of footage, he said, adding: "The actions we have been taking as part of our investigation send a clear warning to anyone intent on causing disruption and disorder at any future events."

Around 500 anti-migrant protesters took to the streets of Portsmouth on Saturday and were met by hundreds of counter-protesters from Stand up to Racism.

Migrants intercepted in the Channel are typically brought to Dover for initial processing.

However, the dinghy that arrived at Eastney Marina had set off from near Cherbourg in the Bay of the Seine, about 170 miles (274km) west of Calais and significantly further west than the usual departure points.

News.title: US embassy child abuse images suspect flown from UK before police interview
News.content:
A US embassy staffer accused of possessing indecent images of children, was detained at his south London flat and flown out of the UK in August, without being first questioned by British police.

The US Embassy confirmed to the BBC that authorities are investigating the allegations and they have reassigned the staff member to the US while inquiries continue.

"The United States government expects all personnel to adhere to the highest standards of conduct, and we take these allegations seriously," embassy officials said in a statement.

They added that they "quickly informed UK law enforcement and took swift action."

It is understood the individual worked at the US embassy in Vauxhall, south west London, and though not a diplomat, he enjoyed the umbrella of diplomatic protection.

He was flown back to the United States on a commercial flight, but their investigations are ongoing in conjunction with UK authorities.

It is also understood Home Office ministers and the Metropolitan Police are in close contact with the US embassy on this matter as investigations continue.

A UK government spokesperson said: "We expect all foreign diplomats in the UK to abide by our laws, in the same way we expect all UK diplomats to do so when posted overseas."

News.title: Tom Felton: I'm so excited to see Rupert Grint play Ron Weasley again
News.content:
Every night on Broadway, Tom Felton walks on stage to a roar from the audience. He had expected the reaction to die down after the first week, but it never did.

Almost 15 years after his final appearance as Draco Malfoy on screen, Felton has spent the past 10 months playing the character again in the Broadway production of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.

I meet the actor in a dressing room at NBC Studios, just off Times Square in New York. He's just finished a live television appearance and in a few hours will be back on stage for his next performance.

He greets me with a hug and says he is excited to speak to BBC News because his mum and 100-year-old grandfather will see it. His family are some of his biggest supporters - his mum has seen the show five times already, while his dad is due to visit next month.

That support mirrors the enthusiasm Felton has encountered from Harry Potter fans, which he says still surprises him more than two decades after he first played Draco.

"I thought the applause would stop in the first week and it has not.

"It's very humbling and lovely to know how much the characters still mean to people now and if it brings them to the theatre, that's the best."

He is also struck by how many of the fans now approaching him were not alive when the first Harry Potter film was released.

"There are fans that approach me shouting 'Draco' who weren't even born when I was in the first film," he says.

News.title: Diljit Dosanjh makes history under the famous Wembley arch
News.content:
On Saturday night, under the world-famous Wembley arch, five words rang out: "Punjabi Aa Gaye Wembley Oye!"

Indian megastar Diljit Dosanjh famously starts all his concerts by announcing that "the Punjabis have arrived".

But this time, it was a play on the usual catchphrase.

Dosanjh is the first ever Punjabi singer to headline Wembley Stadium, the music venue has said.

Addressing his fans, he reflected on the significance of the occasion. "This moment will go down in the history books," he said.

And as Bhangra beats blared out, fans erupted with cheers while Dosanjh launched into his biggest hits, from Born to Shine to Lover.

Over two decades, Dosanjh has built a huge global fanbase, topping charts and singing with the likes of Ed Sheeran.

He has even busted Bhangra moves with Jimmy Fallon, external, with the US talk show host labelling him "the biggest Punjabi artist on the planet".

His landmark concert at Wembley further cements his status as a global star.

Ahead of the show, the singer spoke exclusively to the BBC backstage, describing the moment as "a dream" for him.

News.title: Police probe use of firearm after man found dead in Armadale
News.content:
Police are investigating the use of a firearm after a man was found dead in West Lothian.

Emergency services were called to reports of an injured person in a property on Harestanes Road, Armadale, at about 11:50 on Saturday. A 35-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Police Scotland said inquiries were at an early stage and a post-mortem examination would take place, but one line of inquiry is that a firearm may have been used.

The force is also looking at whether a car fire in the nearby Netherhouses area is linked to the incident.

News.title: Prince William launches £250K fund for village
News.content:
The Prince of Wales is launching a new regeneration fund to support Princetown, the isolated Dartmoor community facing an uncertain future following the closure of Dartmoor Prison.

The Princetown Community Fund will make at least Â£250,000 available to locally led social, economic and environmental projects.

Grants of between Â£500 and Â£40,000 will be distributed through Devon Communities Together, which will also provide support to groups applying for funding.

The fund follows William's decision to stop personally benefiting from the Â£1.5m annual rent generated by Dartmoor Prison, with the funding redirected into the local community.

News.title: Major fire at derelict mill featured in Peaky Blinders and Downton Abbey
News.content:
Another major fire has broken out at a derelict mill complex where Peaky Blinders was filmed.

The blaze at Dalton Mills in Keighley started at about 20:00 BST on Saturday and at its peak required 12 fire engines to tackle it.

West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service (WYFRS) confirmed that due to the severity of the incident a number of nearby residents were evacuated and at 23:00 BST, 10 fire engines were still in attendance.

A spokesperson added: "Members of the public are still advised to avoid the area to allow emergency services to operate safely and effectively."

News.title: Europe must endure winter of hardship to keep pressure on Putin, says PM's security adviser
News.content:
Powell said "we cannot turn that into an advantage for Putin", adding that pressure on Putin was working "and that means we have to keep the pressure up".

"It will require some real hardship and difficulties on our parts," he added. "But we will have to swallow that and we have to keep the economic, military, political and diplomatic support going for Ukraine."

While admitting that things in Ukraine did "feel a bit difficult at the moment", with a lack of Patriot air defence missiles, strikes on businesses and the governments budget deficit, Powell insisted "there are strong reasons for optimism".

He said Trump â who has blown hot and cold on Ukraine â was "in a very different place".

"He sees that Ukraine is doing better and therefore he is not leaning in the direction of Putin in the way that he was previously. I think that's a really big asset."

Powell said Russia was no longer claiming the US had agreed that Ukraine should give up territory and hopes of Nato membership at last year's Trump-Putin summit in Alaska.

"The so-called Anchorage compromise is firmly dead," he said. "We can stop worrying about it. It's finished."

This meant "we can look for serious ways of getting to a negotiated settlement, rather than waiting for the Ukrainian people to hand over territory the Russians have not been able to conquer", Powell said.

Ukrainian commanders had successfully held the front line on the ground while Russia had reached 1.5 million casualties, Ukraine had increasingly struck deep within Russian territory while Europe's resolve remained solid, he noted.

"The strategy is to apply enough pressure to make [Putin] want to get into negotiation," Powell said.

"And I think that the escalation we hear talk about is not a problem - it's a sign of success, because what's happening is the pressure that we are putting on Putin is finally paying off."

Putin himself has given little sign he is feeling under pressure, telling journalists earlier this month: "I have no doubt that the enemy will crumble."

Meanwhile, Ukrainian authorities have begun evacuating some residents in Slovyansk and Kramatorsk, the biggest cities still under full Ukrainian control in the eastern Donbas region. Russia claims sovereignty over the Donbas and fully capturing it is a key objective for Moscow.

Powell said the war was "not about territory" but about "the right of Ukraine to be independent", adding that "to the extent that [Putin] gains another 10km of land or loses another 40km of land, this war is already won".

"That's the threat to him at home. There is a free, independent and European Ukraine, and people in Russia are going to notice that."

The national security adviser said it was a "mug's game" to predict when the war might end, but said Europe had to be prepared to negotiate a settlement.

"Where we least expect it, Putin will be ready to negotiate... It's all about getting him to be serious in that negotiation. And I think that strategy is beginning to work."

Powell, who helped negotiate the Good Friday Agreement in Northern Ireland, said the US and Europe should maintain contact with Putin â despite describing the Russian leader as a "terrorist".

"What we don't want is miscalculation - that they don't understand where our red lines are. That's why I think it's important the CIA went to Moscow as well."

News.title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England following repayment row
News.content:
University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.

Ministers said they would spell out that governments can change repayment rules and that different career choices can affect how much borrowers repay.

They agreed to some but not all of the recommendations made by MPs after an inquiry into student loans, and did not say whether they would reverse a freeze to the repayment threshold for some graduates.

The inquiry found the way loans had been presented to teenagers amounted to mis-selling, after the BBC revealed the Department for Education (DfE) had compared repayments to Â£30-a-month phone contracts.

The recent debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were issued in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales.

The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year. The loans are written off after 30 years.

Campaigners want a lower interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse a decision last year to freeze the threshold at Â£29,385 for three years in England.

Freezing that threshold means graduates start repaying their loans sooner and, once they do, they pay more than they would have done if it had risen with inflation.

MPs on the Treasury Committee called for a U-turn on that decision as part of a series of recommendations after an inquiry this summer.

The Treasury and the DfE did not say whether ministers would unfreeze the threshold in their response, but said: "We keep all aspects of the student finance system under review."

News.title: Man charged with concealing identity at protest
News.content:
A man has been charged with concealing his identity at a protest in Portsmouth, after police warned they would arrest demonstrators using face masks and coverings.

Several hundred anti-migrant protesters marched through the city centre while anti-racism groups also made their way to Guildhall Square on Saturday.

Hampshire Police said Timothy Miller, 76, of Sherwood Avenue in Hedge End was charged with wearing or using an item to conceal identity at a protest. He is due before Portsmouth magistrates on Monday.

David McNally, 33, of Winchester Road in Portsmouth, was also charged with obstructing the highway and attempted criminal damage. He is due in court on 29 October.

Hampshire Police said on Friday it would use new powers under the Crime and Policing Act to prevent protesters wearing face coverings that conceal their identity.

Both sets of demonstrators were kept apart by police when they arrived at Guldhall Square.

The city centre protests followed disorder on 6 September when police attended Eastney Marina as hundreds of demonstrators blocked roads in an attempt to stop coaches carrying 120 migrants, who had crossed the Channel in a dinghy, from leaving the city.

A 16-year-old male from Waterlooville was also arrested at Saturday's protests on suspicion of violent disorder, in relation to the events at Eastney Marina.

He has been released on bail until 12 December.

Del Leon Somerville, 42, from Paulsgrove appeared at Portsmouth Magistrates Court on Saturday charged with violent disorder and assaulting a police officer at the Eastney protest.

He was remanded in custody to appear at Portsmouth Crown Court on 16 September.

News.title: Man charged following armed bus hijacking
News.content:
A 39-year-old man has been charged with a number of offences after a bus was hijacked in County Tyrone on Saturday.

The driver of the bus was threatened at knife point by a man, who then allowed passengers to leave the bus. However, the bus driver was kept on board.

The charges include kidnapping, hijacking, aggravated vehicle taking causing injury and possession of an offensive weapon.

The man will appear before Enniskillen Magistrates Court on Monday.

Videos circulating on social media appeared to show a Translink Goldliner coach being driven at speed through residential streets while being chased by a Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) patrol car.

Police said the bus was hijacked in the Beltany Road area of Omagh, Co Tyrone, shortly before 13:00 BST on Saturday.

The man who hijacked the bus then made off in the direction of Newtownstewart and a pursuit ensued along the A5 through Victoria Bridge and Sion Mills. The pursuit lasted nearly 20 miles.

"The bus was eventually stopped in the Head of the Town area of Strabane and a man, aged in his 30s was removed from the bus and subsequently arrested," said a PSNI spokesperson.

The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service (NIAS) said two people were taken to South West Acute Hospital for treatment.

News.title: Shocked walker finds SUV blocking route on Wales Coast Path
News.content:
Stunned walker Canberk Beker could not believe his eyes when he came across a car blocking his way on the Wales Coast Path.

The 31-year-old was out for a stroll with wife Bethan Jones, also 31, when they saw the blue Kia Sportage on Saturday morning between Mumbles and Langland Bay.

The driver had managed to wedge the SUV between a concrete fence post on one side and a bench on the other.

Canberk, from Langland, in Swansea, said: "It was completely covering the path. I was looking inside the car."

South Wales Police said it did not attend the scene, while a local councillor believes the driver mistakenly drove down a walking path believing to be a road before getting stuck.

Gary Neville has claimed that Manchester United can expect “an apology” from Pro Ref after Erling Haaland’s controversial winner in the Manchester derby.

Haaland scored the only goal of the game as he arrived at the back post to bundle past Senne Lammens in the 60th minute, and while the goal was originally disallowed for offside, it was overturned and awarded to the visitors after a lengthy VAR review.

There was confusion initially over whether Haaland himself was offside when Josko Gvardiol played the cross, though the Norwegian was eventually proved to be in an onside position. However, the positioning of Enzo Fernandez complicated things, with the Argentine having been offside before making an effort to head the ball before it arrived at the feet of Haaland.

Though Fernandez did not touch the ball himself, there was debate over whether he had interfered with play, though the goal was given.

open image in gallery Erling Haaland bundled in in the second half to give 10-man City a memorable away win ( Getty )

“VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded,” said the Premier League Match Centre in a post explaining the decision on X.

City – who were on the end of their own controversial decision after Phil Foden was sent off for kicking Bruno Fernandes in the first half – went on to win the game 1-0, maintaining their 100 percent winning record this season.

Neville insisted that referee Michael Oliver had got the decision for the goal wrong at the time, saying that “the officials will be nervous” and “will recognise they got this wrong”.

And he had not changed his opinion after full-time, with the former United defender insisting that his old club “will see an apology”.

“They're the words that I think – emphatically – means we will see an apology from Pro Ref," said Neville referring to the wording of the offside rule.

open image in gallery The win puts City second, behind Arsenal on goal difference alone ( Reuters )

"There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off. It’s a really strange one. They’ll recognise they got that wrong,” he explained.

The wording of the offside rule states that a player is offside when interfering with an opponent by “preventing an opponent from playing or being able to play the ball by clearly obstructing the opponent’s line of vision”, or “challenging an opponent for the ball”, as well as if a player is “clearly attempting to play a ball which is close when this action impacts on an opponent”.

Neville added that he expects a "massive inquest into the goal, which I think was wrongly given", having also admitted the goal left him so confused that he "needed the offside rule explained to me”.

Fellow pundit Micah Richards agreed, saying that the officials “have got it so wrong,” but adding that it should take nothing away from a solid City performance.

Roy Keane, meanwhile, felt that United were “punished” for holding a strong line.

The win means Maresca’s side remain unbeaten this season, joining Arsenal on 12 points at the summit of the Premier League table.

They are in League Cup action against Norwich City on Thursday, with their final match before the international break coming at home to Sunderland on 20 September.

News.title: US Open final LIVE: Ben Shelton faces Alexander Zverev with grand slam history on the line in New York
News.content:
'I'm the most confident I've ever been in my game' - Shelton ahead of Zverev final

Home hope Ben Shelton bids to make US Open history as the American faces Alexander Zverev in the New York final.

The 23-year-old Shelton is aiming to end the 23-year wait for an American man to triumph at the US Open, since Andy Roddick lifted the title in 2003. Shelton is also aiming to became the first Black man to win the US Open since Arthur Ashe since 1968, and will do so in the stadium that is named after the iconic Ashe.

Standing in Shelton’s way is the top seed Zverev, who is bidding to become a two-time grand slam champion in the season where the German made his breakthrough at the age of 29 at the French Open. Zverev, who was also beaten by Jannik Sinner in the Wimbledon final in July, has won all five of his previous matches with Shelton.

The American will have the home support this time, however, after an inspired late-night victory over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals. After returning to beat his good friend Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals on Friday, Shelton is now just one win away from writing his name in the record books.

The by-election to replace Sir Keir Starmer is being used as a test run for Andy Burnham to decide whether to pull the trigger on an early general election, Labour sources have told The Independent.

The Holborn and St Pancras contest, widely expected to be held on 8 October, was called after Sir Keir called an immediate end to his parliamentary career earlier this month, after being ousted as prime minister and Labour leader.

But with Green leader Zack Polanski now standing in the seat as a candidate, The Independent has been told Labour strategists around Mr Burnham say it will be a clear test of whether the change of leadership has killed off the rising threat to the party from the Greens.

Labour has selected Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali, who came to the UK as a child refugee, as their candidate for the seat.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham is thought to be considering an early election (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA Wire )

But the party is still haunted by the Green candidate Hannah Spencer beating them into third place, with Reform second, in the ultra-safe Gorton and Denton seat earlier this year.

A party source told The Independent: “Because Keir’s seat was a target and Polanski is running in it, this gives the PM a perfect opportunity to see if the Green threat has gone with a change of leader.

“We are seeing people come back [from the Greens] to Labour. Under Keir, there was no doubt that we were losing lots of supporters and party members to the Greens.”

They added: “If we can beat Polanski in a by-election it will show that Labour is in good shape to fight a general election.”

It was noted by another source that the decision to sanction Israeli settlers and take a firmer stance against the Netanyahu government had “nullified some of the Green appeal” to Labour voters.

“This by-election will be a test of that,” they added.

open image in gallery Green leader Zack Polanski will be his party’s candidate ( AFP/Getty )

It could mean an unusual November election which would be the earliest after a by-election in October.

But Downing Street has pointed out that Mr Burnham told the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg at the beginning of September that he would not call an early election.

He said: “I’m going to rule it out... I don't think people want it.”

Subsequently, a Number 10 source added: “This is complete nonsense, the PM has ruled out an early election.”

But it comes amid growing speculation that Mr Burnham could go for a snap poll in November with tricky decisions on tax and spend ahead of him and a lack of mandate as prime minister, bound by Sir Keir’s manifesto.

While polling experts including professor Sir John Curtice have warned against an early election because the “Burnham bounce” has not been enough to give Labour a big enough lead, the prospect of one is still understood to be under consideration.

This has been fuelled by Whitehall sources saying that civil servants have been handed training on running the country without a government – which usually refers to the period of a general election when parliament is not sitting.

Already, other parties are preparing for an early election, with Reform claiming the £72m it received this week from two crypto billionaires is to fund an election war chest with the expectation Mr Burnham plans to call one in the coming months.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has also requested a pre-election briefing of the government books by civil servants on the basis that there may be an early poll.

Another source said that Sir Keir may have been encouraged to quit early so they could use his seat to test whether an early election was feasible.

They said: “Labour advisers are using the by-election result as the decider on calling a snap this year or not.

open image in gallery Labour candidate for Holborn and St Pancras Sagal Abdi-Wali ( Getty )

“One suggested this was thought up as a ‘poll-proof fail-safe’ around early August, and then led to pushing Starmer to resign and using his seat for various reasons. The others have said that this came about as a result of Starmer resigning, and seeing an opportunity to determine the board at play.”

It is understood, though, that Labour believes the Burnham honeymoon period is “going better than expected”, with policies, such as removing VAT from energy bills and capping bus fares to £2, going down well with voters. But they fear it is coming to an end.

Polls also show a lead for Labour over scandal-hit Reform, while the Tories under Ms Badenoch continue to struggle with their share of the support in the late teens.

On Saturday, pollsters Opinium put Labour on 27 per cent, Reform 25 per cent and the Tories on 19 per cent. The Greens are on 11 per cent, well below the level they hit when Sir Keir was leader.

Meanwhile, Mr Burnham has a +5 leader rating, Ms Badenoch +1, Mr Polanski is now at -22, and Mr Farage -26.

Mr Polanski, though, believes he can pull off a victory in the constituency, saying he is “incredibly confident” about winning in Holborn and St Pancras.

Speaking to The Independent, he said: “This by-election is first and foremost about the people of Holborn and St Pancras, and whether they want to be represented by another Labour backbencher who will toe the party line, or if they want a bold Green MP who will fight for them and push the government to be better.

“People want to see an MP who can force action on affordable housing and the cost of living – not be used as pawns in some wider Westminster game. Andy Burnham has been talking about the issue of housing but ruled out rent controls. He’s ruled out bringing water companies into full public ownership.

“The real test for this Labour government is whether they have the courage to deliver real solutions.”
