Robert Jenrick has hit back at Donald Trump’s calls for a united Ireland and said the US President should have “butted out” of British politics.

Reform UK’s treasury spokesman said Trump “shouldn’t have weighed into British politics” when he claimed Irish reunification was inevitable and it “may as well happen now”, during a visit to Dublin on Saturday.

Mr Jenrick told Sky News’s Sunday Morning programme: “If you’re referring to what he said about Ireland he was completely wrong.

“We’re a unionist party. The clue’s in the name, Reform UK, and we’ll always support the union.

“We firmly disagree with Donald Trump on this. He shouldn’t have weighed into British politics. Our borders are our borders. And Reform will always defend the United Kingdom.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump claimed Irish reunification was inevitable during his visit to Dublin ( PA )

Angela Rayner brushed off Mr Trump’s comments, saying the UK remained committed to the Good Friday Agreement.

The Housing Secretary told Sky News: “Donald Trump is Donald Trump, and the president will say what and speak his mind as he sees it.

“But look, we’re really serious about the Good Friday Agreement.

“We’re very proud of our history there and working with Ireland to make sure that we implement the Good Friday Agreement and we continue on that path.”

During a visit to Dublin on Saturday, Mr Trump said he would “love” to see a united Ireland.

Speaking while sitting alongside Taoiseach Micheál Martin, the US president said: “Well, I don’t want to cause any problems, but I will tell you I’d love to see it unified.

“I have friends on both sides, great people. They’re Irish people. How can they be bad, right? I’d love to see it unified. I think it would be a great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. It’s going to happen eventually.

“You know what? The way I look at it, it’s going to happen eventually. It may as well happen now.

open image in gallery Mr Trump during a meeting with Taoiseach Micheál Martin at Farmleigh House, Dublin ( PA Wire )

“We’re talking about it and you got the right man over here to get it moving. But, yeah, I think it would be a fantastic thing.

“Now the UK will have something to say about it, obviously. But I think it would be a great thing. I mean, how can it be bad?”

The US President’s opinions triggered a major diplomatic row, with unionist leaders in Northern Ireland, members of Reform and the Conservative party all disagreeing with his view.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage wrote on X: “Northern Ireland is a proud and integral part of the United Kingdom. The people of Northern Ireland neither want a referendum, nor unification. I disagree with President Trump.”

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Trump is “shooting from the hip as usual” and creating “unnecessary tension” following his comments on a united Ireland.

“This sort of loose talk about the future of democratic countries is deeply unhelpful and creates unnecessary tension. Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom,” she wrote in a post on X.

open image in gallery Mr Trump gestures as he is welcomed by Ireland's president Catherine Connolly at Áras an Uachtaráin in Phoenix Park in the Irish capital Dublin ( AFP/Getty )

The shadow secretary of state for Northern Ireland also said Mr Trump’s comments were “very wrong”.

Conservative MP Alex Burghart said: “Northern Ireland is an integral part of the United Kingdom. Kemi and the Conservatives will always stand up for the Union.

“We will build a stronger economy in every corner of the United Kingdom, creating jobs and opportunities and clearing up Labour’s mess.”

DUP leader Gavin Robinson said Northern Ireland’s future would be decided by its people, not “commentary in London, Dublin or Washington”.

He added: “As unionists, we are not interested in the destruction of our country by joining with the Irish Republic.”

While he was on a university field trip in 2022, the boat in which Joseph Nguthiru was traversing Kenya’s Lake Naivasha suddenly came to a halt. It became tangled up in water hyacinth, an invasive plant that covers much of the water. Here, he and his fellow classmates in the boat were forced to sit for five long hours.

The hyacinth, which has been a problem in Kenya since the late 1980s, floats on the top of water, like a thick carpet and it can double in size in just a few days. It blocks oxygen from getting into the water, effectively making the area beneath it barren, killing aquatic life.

To win tickets to see Bel Trew’s latest compelling documentary click here

In some places, the hyacinth is so thick, engines need to be turned off and a long pole is used to pull boats through it.

Joseph, aged 28, says everyone in Kenya knows about the phenomenon, but it wasn’t until this trip that he’d “experienced the pain behind the people who face it every day”. The weeds mean it’s becoming almost impossible to fish here, which was a thriving industry and an important food source for local communities.

Joseph describes that day as a “crazy experience” but it left him thinking there must be a way to use this invasive plant, and help unclog the vital waterways.

People see the rubbish, but they don’t even have the time to think or to do anything about it. People have bigger problems to solve where I come from

Inspired, Joseph took some of the water hyacinth back to Egerton University, where he was studying civil engineering, and specialised in water and environmental engineering. He decided to base his final-year project on finding a solution for it. It took plenty of trial and error, but he turned it into a bioplastic, which was something the country needed after banning single-use plastic in 2017, and the project was a success.

Joseph went on to form HyaPak, a startup turning the invasive water hyacinth into biodegradable packaging. His work earned him the East Africa Youth for Climate Action Award, and he was named a Young Champion of the Earth, as part of the United Nations Environmental Programme. He’s also become a leader at the Obama Foundation, and was made a Presidential Awardee for Best Innovator in Kenya and included on the Africa 40 Under 40 list.

It wasn’t only that day on the lake that inspired him, though. He grew up in the Eastlands side of Nairobi, where he says, “one of the things you’re constantly exposed to is pollution, as there’s a lot of trash lying around”. Here, people have different problems, from paying rent and getting children into education, so pollution is a secondary problem. “You see it, but you don’t even have the time to think or to do anything about it. People have bigger problems to solve where I come from.”

And Joseph is aware that plenty of human-made waste ends up in the water. “The thing about humans is that we are really good at pollution, especially making trash go into water. So chemical waste, agricultural runoff, and even urban waste, some way or another, ends up in water bodies, and hyacinth derives from this.”

Anywhere you see water hyacinth, the water is polluted

The lake is also on the edge of one of Kenya’s biggest rose farming areas and it’s thought chemicals from the farms end up in the river, though they have started using closed-loop water systems which helps prevent this.

Water hyacinth is an indicator of those pollution problems. “Anywhere you see hyacinth, the water is polluted,” he says.

It’s technically easy to remove, as it just floats on water, but the issue is that after removing it, 6-12 days later, it will have grown back. “It’s one of the world’s fastest-growing plants,” Joseph says, explaining that the issue is they have to keep on removing it over and over again.

So far, HyaPak has removed about 20 acres (eight hectares) of water hyacinth, according to its latest annual figures at the end of 2025. Though its regrowth speed makes it hard to calculate accurately.

For this reason, Joseph doesn’t like to think of HyaPak as “removing” the weeds, as it gives the impression it’s being eliminated and won’t come back. But that’s almost impossible to do, given the speed it grows. Instead, he prefers to look at it as managing it. “We need to utilise it for something that has a value and a benefit to the people and communities that you’re working with,” he says.

open image in gallery Aged just 28, Nguthiru has already been recognised by some of the world’s leading awards for his enviromental work ( HyaPak )

It’s a bad problem fundamentally, but for Joseph, turning it on its head, he’s able to see how removing the weeds and replacing bioplastics feed each other. Finding a commercial use for this fast-growing weed also helps create what he calls “green jobs” – something that actually facilitates the world’s transition into a circular economy.

“We work with the fishing community and they collect the water hyacinth for us,” he explains, which both men and women do. For many of the people living here, they’re below the World Bank’s poverty line. By being able to add an extra source of revenue to the community, Joseph thinks this is “the best way to go about any social innovation”, plus it gives hope and dignity to people.

Once harvested, the weeds are dried on the side of the lake, then sent to HyaPak’s facility in Nairobi. They’re then crushed into a fine powder, the cellulose is extracted and is used to make different types of packaging materials. These include courier packages where HyaPak is working with one of the world’s largest courier companies to transition their packaging away from plastic, and liners for boxes, which help keep food fresher for 2-3 days longer without the need for cold storage.

But one of the biggest uses is more unexpected. In 2022, Kenya launched Jaza Miti, a huge tree-planting target, set by the president, Wiliam Ruto, to plant 15 billion trees over 10 years.

“It’s a crazy target,” Joseph says, breaking it down to meaning 4.1 million trees would need to be planted each day. But it’s a target he admires. “If you’re planting 15 billion trees, you need 15 billion packaging bags for those trees. Overnight, there was huge demand [for bioplastic replacements] that didn’t exist before,” he says. Now HyaPak makes bioplastic alternatives that cover the root system of seedling trees before they’re planted, and then decompose directly into the soil. Of course, HyaPak’s unable to meet such huge targets, but it is scaling up to work towards the demand.

Joseph’s plan now is to also try to scale the business in other countries suffering from the same invasive species, such as El Salvador, India, South Africa and then onto Mexico and Nigeria. It’s largely been made possible to imagine after winning the UN’s Young Champion of the Earth award, which really took HyaPak to the world stage.

As well as HyaPak, Joseph’s also co-founded M-SITU, which uses solar-powered artificial intelligence sensors to detect deforestation, wildfires and illegal charcoal burning. He created a small water-bottle-size detector, using 3D printing, that scans a radius up to 1km around it looking for illegal loggers or wildfires, so it can alert rangers. A pilot scheme in Kenya’s Ngong Forest cut ranger response times from six hours to 15 minutes.

All from one day getting stuck on a boat in a mass of invasive weeds, Joseph has turned a problem into a resource – and, in doing so, found a way to make the very thing clogging Kenya’s waterways part of the solution, providing value and jobs along the way.

Shane Lowry produced another golfing masterclass for a final round 63 as the home favourite cruised to a record 11-shot win on 23 under at the Amgen Irish Open.

The 39-year-old, who shot a course-record 62 on Friday, teed off on Sunday with a four-shot lead in front of Taoiseach Micheal Martin and went on to make eight more birdies to dominate the field.

As his closest challengers, Dane Jacob Skov Olesen and Chilean Joaquin Niemann, failed to make in-roads on the final day at the Trump International Golf Links and Hotel in Doonbeg, Lowry maintained his red-hot putting form.

He sank huge 45-feet efforts at the seventh and 15th holes and sealed his second Irish Open triumph in style, 17 years after first winning it as an amateur in 2009, with another superb birdie putt at the last hole.

Lowry told Sky Sports: “To come here this week and do this, like come on! I don’t know. I just don’t do things by half measures.

“I can’t believe I’m standing here, (looking at) that leaderboard. My God! I didn’t know how I was doing. I said to my caddie after holing 15, ‘How far ahead are we?’ He said, ‘Far enough’. So I was happy with that.

“A lot of things went right for me. But this has been the most spectacular week. It’s just mad. I can’t believe it. My mum’s just standing there, it’s been unreal.”

America’s 2018 Masters champion Patrick Reed emerged from the trailing pack to finish tied for second alongside Niemann on 12 under after making six birdies for a faultless final-round 64.

Niemann birdied two of the final five holes for a 67 and Denmark’s Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen carded a superb bogey-free 63, which included an eagle at the fifth, to finish third on 11 under.

Northern Ireland’s Tom McKibben ended an impressive week as he made a final-round 67 to finish on 10 under, tied for fifth alongside Gregorio De Leo after the Italian made a bogey-free 63.

England’s Alex Fitzpatrick made seven birdies and two bogeys for a 65 for a share of seventh place with Olesen, while Lowry’s close friend Rory McIlroy closed with a 67 to finish tied in 41st place on one under.

Lowry, whose last individual win was at the BMW PGA Championship in 2022, had extended his lead to four shots in front of watching United States President Donald Trump on Saturday.

The Irishman also won the 2019 Open on home soil, at Royal Portrush Golf Club in County Antrim.

Lowry added: “My wife and my kids are back in Florida. When things are not going well at this level, it’s hard at home as well, but my wife has been a huge support and my kids, I love them so much.

“I’m so happy for them. I can’t wait to bring a trophy home. My daughter is always asking, when are you going to bring a trophy home. So I’m going to bring a trophy home.”

Lando Norris has challenged Formula One to change a “stupid rule” after he was cruelly denied victory at Sunday’s Spanish Grand Prix.

Kimi Antonelli took a major stride towards becoming the sport’s youngest world champion after he capitalised on Lance Stroll putting his Aston Martin in the wall to earn a free pit-stop during a Virtual Safety Car period and claim his eighth victory from the 14 rounds so far.

While fortune was on Antonelli’s side, Norris’ luck was out. The world champion was comfortably leading when Stroll crashed on the 14th lap.

But Norris drove past the pit-lane entry just as the VSC was deployed. Norris stopped on the next lap and a slow front-right tyre change lost the British driver even more time.

Having held a seven-second advantage over Antonelli prior to Stroll’s accident, Norris left the pits 13 seconds adrift of the Italian.

Norris began to demonstrate the speed in his McLaren that should have won him the race, and with 10 laps left he was one second behind Max Verstappen and just two seconds adrift of Antonelli.

But with overtaking impossible at this new street venue on the outskirts of the Spanish capital, Norris had to settle for third. He is now 106 points back and his hopes of defending his world crown all but over.

“We didn’t do anything that made us lose the race,” a deflated Norris said. “We were just insanely unlucky today.

“I was the only one on the whole grid who didn’t get a chance to do a pit-stop.

open image in gallery Kimi Antonelli celebrates his victory (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

“That is just unfortunate. It has happened in races before, and I have gained from it in the past, but I have lost a win today and that is frustrating. I felt like I deserved more.

“It just hurts because there was nothing more I could do as a driver. I got pole, I led the race, and to lose it for nothing in my control is not how a race should be won.”

Pressed as to whether the rulebook should be tinkered, Norris continued: “It has been brought up many times over the years by different drivers.

“There are things that can be changed to make it more simple, and more fair. We could be covered for at least one lap (after the VSC is deployed) and that allows us all the opportunity to do a pit-stop, or the pit-entry could be blocked.

“This needs to be part of a wider discussion, and as a group of drivers, I think it is something we would all want. I have to take it on the chin today, but I hope it doesn’t happen to anyone again, because it is not the way a race should be lost.”

In a TV interview, Norris described it as a “stupid rule”.

open image in gallery Kimi Antonelli (second right) celebrates winning the Spanish Grand Prix, alongside Max Verstappen (left) and Norris (right) (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

Norris headed into Sunday’s inaugural fixture at the Madring with two wins from his last three appearances and, as he built a comfortable lead, a championship comeback might have been on his mind.

But the mood changed when Stroll crashed. Could McLaren have foreseen the VSC and pulled their man in a lap earlier?

“I will speak to the team,” he said. “But it is not the team’s fault, and it is not my fault. It’s as simple as that.”

Antonelli’s second win in a week – after his remarkable comeback display from 19th in Monza – puts him firmly on course to drive into the history books and usurp Sebastian Vettel (who was 23 when he claimed his first title in 2010) as the sport’s youngest champion.

He is 81 points clear in the standings after George Russell finished a disappointing fifth in the other Mercedes.

“It is great, but we have to keep pushing, keep delivering and trying to do the best job I can,” Antonelli said.

“Of course, it is a big lead, but you never know what can happen so I have to be ready for everything.”

Erling Haaland‘s derby winner for Manchester City against Manchester United was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernandez appearing to interfere with play from an offside position.

Haaland’s controversial goal on the hour-mark earned the 10-man visitors victory at Old Trafford after Phil Foden was sent off early in the first half of the Premier League clash.

Haaland was initially ruled to be offside when he tucked in Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross from the left wing to put City 1-0 up.

However, to much confusion, the striker was then ruled to be onside following a lengthy check from the VAR Matt Donohue.

Haaland was played onside by Patrick Dorgu’s outstretched foot as the Manchester United defender went to close down Gvardiol and attempted to block the cross.

The angle of the initial TV replays appeared to show that Haaland was in an offside position at the back post.

But the Premier League’s semi-automated offside technology proved that Haaland was in fact behind Dorgu.

Was Enzo Fernandez interfering with play from an offside position?

The reason the check too so long was because Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position in the penalty box as he also attempted to reach the cross. The Manchester City midfielder made a move to reach the cross with a diving header, but missed the ball.

The Premier League Match Centre confirmed: “VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball.”

The rules of the game state that a player stood in an offside position will be penalised if they are:

Preventing an opponent from playing or being able to play the ball by clearly obstructing the opponent's line of vision; or

Challenging an opponent for the ball; or

Clearly attempting to play a ball which is close when this action impacts on an opponent; or

Making an obvious action which clearly impacts on the ability of an opponent to play the ball.

There is an argument that Fernandez put off the United defender Lisandro Martinez, who was between Fernandez and Haaland at the back post.

If Fernandez was not in the box, Martinez would have been expected to clear the cross, or goalkeeper Senne Lammens could have come to collect it.

The VAR, however, must have decided that Fernandez attempting to play the ball did not impact on Martinez’s ability to clear Gvardiol’s cross.

open image in gallery There was confusion and a long delay before Haalands’ goal was awarded ( Reuters )

City were down to 10 men in the Manchester derby following Foden’s first-half red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

Haaland’s ninth league goal against United means the striker is now top scorer in the Manchester derbies in the Premier League.

News.title: Redemption Sunday for Hull and Woad as Europe reclaim Solheim Cup
News.content:
The quiet but steely 22-year-old, who everyone seemed to have forgotten was a rookie, punched her fist when she held the decisive two-footer, before the customary hug with opponent Auston Kim and then being mobbed by her team.

“This was really important,” Woad said. “I mean, I was pretty disappointed and felt like I was kind of letting everyone down. Then the captain kind of spoke to me and said that I was third on [the most] birdies [made]. So I just had to trust that and that’s golf sometimes. And it ended up I got the winning putt.”

Some will claim that Woad was only the match-winner on a technicality. Carlota Ciganda in the penultimate game had not finished off her win against Jennifer Kupcho, but when Woad tapped in, the Spaniard was three up with three to go and was guaranteed a half. So the acclaim Woad received was granted. Not that anyone in the Europe camp cared.

The previous evening they had returned to their team room feeling slightly down that they did not hold the advantage, Kupcho holing a 91-footer on the 17th and a 30-footer on the 18th to deny Ciganda and Céline Boutier. And their mood was not helped when videos appeared on social media of the Americans taking crates of beer on to the bus back to their hotel. Yet that foolish scenario only offered extra incentive. “At least we’ll be the ones taking crates of beer on to our bus this evening,” Mel Reid, the assistant captain, said quite pointedly.

News.title: Antonelli wins Spanish GP to extend title lead after Norris misfortune
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix, the first time the race has been held at the all-new, purpose-built street circuit, the Madring. The track has developed a reputation in its short life for being a bit of a tricky one. Some have gone so far as to call it a “car killer”? Is it living up to that reputation? Probably, especially if you look at some of the lower formulae that have run on it.

It has also increasingly become the case for the Formula One cars, too. The first couple of practice sessions on Friday revealed little to worry about. As the drivers began to push, though, from final practice and qualifying, the mistakes and crashes happened. The biggest so far was Oliver Bearman but also a smaller one for Lewis Hamilton.

There will almost certainly be some kind of incident in the race, but whether we see red flags, safety cars and so on remains to be seen. A bigger and perhaps more significant question will be how much overtaking will take place on this track. The drivers are not optimistic. The theory goes that if tyre degradation is high then there will be, because you will have significant pace offsets between worn and fresh tyres. The problem is that the leaders tend not to differ to greatly from one another on strategy these days...

Perhaps George Russell, who qualified down in sixth and has little to lose, will be brave and put on a set of hard tyres to start with. Russell has work to do yet again. He was not miles off Antonelli in qualifying when it came to pace, but given how close it was in the top six, finds four cars between himself and the championship leader, who just missed out on pole to McLaren’s Lando Norris.

Norris said it was the best lap of his life and seemed to come from nowhere. He improved more than a second from Q2 to Q3 and continues his fine form in 2026. He will start alongside Antonelli with Max Verstappen in third, Lewis Hamilton in fourth and Charles Leclerc in fifth, before Russell.

News.title: Tora Bora’s last midwife struggles under Taliban rule as aid runs dry
News.content:
The small clinic, crowded with pregnant women, sits in the shadow of Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan. Twenty-five years ago, those mountains commanded the attention of the world’s most powerful military. Roughly 15 miles from the clinic, in the Tora Bora cave complex, Osama bin Laden was believed to be hiding as American bombs rained down in the hunt for the architect of 9/11.

Today, another consequence of the West’s long entanglement with Afghanistan is playing out beneath those same mountains – in the struggle to keep mothers and babies alive.

In the baking courtyard of Gandab Kharoti health centre, dozens of women enveloped in sapphire blue burqas sit shoulder to shoulder beneath trees waiting to see Shila Ibrahimi, a 27-year-old midwife.

The women rest against walls, dusty, barefoot children play, and mothers cradle sick babies beneath folds of cloth. Some have walked for hours through the mountains to reach her.

Among them is Fawzia, 30, seven-and-a-half months pregnant with her seventh child. Suffering from headaches, she has walked for miles through the heat.

Her husband works far from the village, so she makes the journey with her children and mother-in-law, hoping the Taliban do not stop her for the “crime” of travelling without a male escort.

Under the Taliban’s morality rules, women face restrictions on travelling alone, while UN monitors have documented the regime’s morality inspectors ordering some health facilities not to treat unaccompanied women.

But enforcement varies and Fawzia says nobody challenged her on her journey here. Asked where she would give birth if the clinic closed she says: “We have nowhere else to go. We cannot afford that. We are poor.”

News.title: Springboks look like World Cup champions elect… again
News.content:
In doing so, Erasmus while still relying on his veteran performers, managed to expose some of the next generation to invaluable white heat pressure, including Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg and Cameron Hanekom, who all look to the manor born.

And the substance of the series victory is heightened by the fact it came against a regenerated and rejuvenated All Blacks side, who rediscovered their high-octane and relentless attacking identity under new coach Dave Rennie. At times the handling and precision of the All Blacks were so sumptuous that it felt like they might be in a position to level the series in Baltimore.

But the narrative of the previous two Tests continued. At key moments they were let down by their discipline and turnovers in attack to gift the Springboks’ transition ball, and their directness, backed by their power both in collisions and set piece enabled them to pick up points much more easily than their opponents.

At the end, the scoreboard ran away from the All Blacks, which was harsh on them. But one had wondered if they would be able to maintain their intensity at the end of the first half, when it took 32 phases for Will Jordan to score a try to cut the deficit to three points.

News.title: Sabalenka smashes racket and swears at cameraman after Rybakina clinches US Open
News.content:
Sabalenka and Rybankina have now played four slam finals, with the spoils evenly shared after this 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 grapple in the Apple – as a boxing promoter might have referred to it.

There is certainly something pugilistic about the way these two go toe-to-toe. The emphasis is on landing the first blow, so the rallies tend not to be particularly long: only four points out of 193 went beyond nine shots. But the precision of the ball-striking was breathtaking. At one point in the first set, Rybakina had hit eight winners to just a single unforced error – the sort of ratio to send coaches starry-eyed.

Sabalanka arrived on court in her showy jewellery – which is worth more than £300,000 for the full set, according to the manufacturers – and an orange Nike dress that put one in mind of the Dutch national football team. “Total tennis” may have been the goal, but sometimes your opponent doesn’t allow you to play. This was the case in the early stages as Rybakina – whose own yellow-and-black outfit evoked the natural warning signs of a wasp or hornet – seemed to flush every ball right out of the centre of her racket.

Sabalenka actually did a sterling job of digging herself out of trouble in her service games, saving four of five break points in the first set. But this still wasn’t enough, given that Rybakina was defending her own serve with the same serenity that characterises everything she does.

News.title: Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Kick off 8pm.

News.title: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players
News.content:
Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

Sports.title: Haaland scores controversial derby winner for Man City after Foden red
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's contentious winner earned 10-man Manchester City a derby win over rivals United at Old Trafford - after Phil Foden's controversial first-half red card.

City have now joined Arsenal as Premier League title race pace setters with maximum points from four games - but their winning goal against Man Utd will be questioned. Enzo Fernandez looked to impact play when clearly in an offside position - but the goal was not ruled out.

City will feel justice was done after their job became much harder when Foden was given his marching orders earlier.

A tepid first half of the 199th Manchester derby was dominated by Foden's shock sending-off. After United captain Bruno Fernandes kicked the ball into his midriff, Foden was adjudged to have reacted by kicking back at the Portuguese.

"VAR has described it as a kick with both feet into the stomach," said Gary Neville on co-commentary.

Whether there was enough contact from Foden to cross the violent conduct threshold will be debated. Whether Fernandes should have also seen red for kicking out at Foden first will also be talked about.

Despite the man advantage, United struggled to use their dominance to full effect. They did hit the post twice through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo - but when Haaland is on the other team, City always have a chance.

That came true as he tapped home at the back post, yet the offside flag went up. The semi-automated offside technology ruled Haaland onside so the goal was given - but Enzo Fernandez being clearly offside and trying to get on the end of the same cross was also approved by VAR.

Foden was shown a straight red card in the first half at Old Trafford for kicking out at Fernandes after being fouled by the Man Utd midfielder.

Speaking immediately after the incident, Sky Sports' Gary Neville said he was "surprised" Fernandes avoided any punishment after appearing to kick Foden first.

Sports.title: Dominant Lowry storms to record 11-stroke triumph at Irish Open
Sports.content:
Shane Lowry stormed to a record 11-shot victory at the Amgen Irish Open, the home crowd favourite shooting a seven-under 63 on Sunday to finish a staggering 23 under par.

It's Lowry's seventh title of his career, and his second success at the Irish Open after his 2009 triumph as a 22-year-old amateur.

It's a welcome return to the winner's circle for Lowry after some agonising near-misses earlier this season, when double-bogeying the last to lose the Dubai Invitational by two strokes, and when letting a three-stroke lead with three to play slip at the Cognizant Classic courtesy of two closing doubles.

The result was never in doubt on Sunday at the Trump International Links in Doonbeg, however, as Lowry - holding a four-shot lead overnight - only increased his winning margin with a fine final round.

Jacob Skov Olesen, his closest challenger at 12 under, four back, would fall away down the leaderboard with a three-over closing 73, while impressive though Patrick Reed's closing 64 and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen's 63 were, seeing them finish tied second and third respectively, Lowry had already surged clear.

Lowry carded eight birdies and just the lone bogey at the ninth, with a couple of stunning 45-footers holed at the par-three seventh and par-four 15th stirring the watching crowd into a frenzy and only surpassed by another birdie holed from distance at 18 to finish things off in some style.

The 39-year-old had taken such a sizeable advantage into Sunday in large part thanks to breaking the course record with a second-round 62 on Friday,

Joaquin Niemann took a share of second with Reed on 12 under, with Neergaard-Petersen one back.

England's Alex Fitzpatrick was tied-seventh at nine under, a closing 64 from Sergio Garcia had him six under, on the same score as Robert MacIntyre and Matt Wallace, among others.

Jon Rahm finished four under and reigning champion Rory McIlroy rounded off a disappointing week with his best round of 67 to end his title defence one under.

Sports.title: What we learned from first Old Firm clash of season
Sports.content:
Rangers dominated Celtic in the first Old Firm clash of the season - of that there is no doubt.

Dan Neil's two perfectly precise strikes from the edge of the area and Kevin Kelsy's back-post volley were symptomatic of the level of control that Derek McInnes' side enjoyed in the game.

Aggressive, front-footed, confident - they were everything that Martin O'Neill's side were not.

Ahead of the second meeting between the two sides in the space of a week - live on Sky Sports - here is what we learned from the first clash of the new season.

McInnes got his tactics right

The Rangers boss humbly shrugged off any suggestion of a tactical masterplan in his post-match news conference - but he was just being modest.

McInnes got his game plan spot on, and Celtic couldn't live with his team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rangers manager Derek McInnes praises his players as they beat Celtic in the first Old Firm clash of the season to progress to the League Cup semi-finals

He used left-back James Penrice as an auxiliary midfielder to flood the middle of the pitch - allowing Rangers to press Celtic man-for-man.

Djeidi Gassama and Minsu Kim provided width and energy as wing-backs with Dujon Sterling, Emmanuel Fernandez and Olwethu Makhanya defending three-vs-three against Celtic's front line.

It was a bold decision that paid dividends as Celtic folded under the pressure.

Image: Rangers impressed against their Old Firm rivals

Dan Neil snatched the starring role of midfield general from his Celtic counterpart Callum McGregor, who was left isolated without a defensive-minded midfield partner.

The former Sunderland man would probably have still been named Player of the Match even if he had not netted two famous derby goals.

Celtic crumble in another big game

Image: Captain Callum McGregor (L) tried to calm the players after conceding a third at Ibrox

After Rangers scored their third, Celtic's usually imperious captain McGregor ordered his own defence "no more goals".

A sobering submission from a figurehead who has been the heartbeat of so many Old Firm victories - but perhaps a signal of a deeper-rooted problem.

Celtic are leaking goals at an alarming rate in big games.

Their now infamous precipitous collapse against LASK from 4-0 up in their Champions League play-off round qualifier is no longer an anomaly. In the two biggest games of Celtic's season so far, they have shipped nine consecutive goals without reply.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic manager Martin O'Neill reacts to their 3-0 defeat to Rangers in the League Cup quarter-finals

A team that has been lauded for the strength of their mentality and togetherness is now showing early signs of mental fragility when faced with the intangible pressure of a 'big game', and the very tangible threat of aggressive, direct and physical opposition.

While Sunday's defeat is nowhere near as humiliating as that fateful evening in Linz, it must serve as a wake-up call for the Scottish champions if they dared to believe they could canter to another title.

Next week just got bigger

Image: There were no Celtic fans allowed at Ibrox

There were no away fans inside Ibrox on Sunday, and there will also be no travelling support at Celtic Park next weekend.

It's impossible to measure what, if any, impact that had on Celtic's lacklustre display or Rangers' rampant performance. However, the result heaps pressure on next week's hosts, who will be met by 60,000 scarred supporters expecting a response.

On paper, the champions go into the game with a 100 percent league record, but psychologically, their impressive start pales in significance to the trauma inflicted upon them following a beating at the hands of their fiercest rivals.

Perhaps the Hoops will embody the spirit of a wounded animal, perhaps Rangers will too crumble without the safety net of their own support, or perhaps any logical or rational thinking applied to attempting to predict the outcome of an Old Firm game will once again be rendered useless.

The only certainty is that next week's Scottish Premiership meeting - live on Sky Sports - is more consequential. Ahead of a three-week-long international break, the gap at the top of the table will stand at either two, five or eight points.

Sports.title: Antonelli wins Spanish GP after luckless Norris loses out
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli took another step in his quest towards winning the 2026 world championship by benefitting from pit-stop misfortune for Lando Norris to win the first Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring.

McLaren's Norris had looked in control of the race after converting his superb pole position into a comfortable early race lead but the battle for victory turned on a lap-14 Virtual Safety Car when Aston Martin's Lance Stroll stopped in a run-off area.

With a VSC offering the field the chance of a so-called 'cheap' pit stop, McLaren were unable to pit Norris immediately as the Briton had just passed the pit-lane entry road.

But the following Antonelli and Verstappen had not, allowing Mercedes and Red Bull to pit their drivers respectively while Norris was running to a controlled reduced speed on track while marshals moved Stroll's car.

McLaren did pit Norris at the end of the next lap but, by then, the VSC had ended, meaning the field was back up to racing speed, with that misfortune then compounded by a slow seven-second service at the tyre change.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris lost the race lead after an unlucky sequence of events which saw a missed a pitstop opportunity under a VSC, followed by a very slow stop by McLaren

Norris rejoined in fifth place and, underlining his prodigious pace, eventually finished on second-placed Verstappen's tail in third but was tantalisingly unable to find a way past the Red Bull through the closing laps.

With George Russell finishing only fifth in the second Mercedes behind a long-running Ferrari of Charles Leclerc, Antonelli's title lead grows to a season-high 81 points with a scheduled nine races remaining.

Antonelli said: "I think today it's good to win but it doesn't feel as good because I think Lando today deserved the win but overall, we take it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was forced to retire early at the Spanish Grand Prix

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton is now 101 points back and all but out of contention after he suffered his first race retirement of the season after his car ran into terminal brake issues inside seven laps.

Liam Lawson was sixth for Red Bull with Alpine's Franco Colapinto seventh ahead of Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren. Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad was ninth with Audi's Nico Hulkenberg in 10th.

Spanish GP Result: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Lando Norris, McLaren



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) George Russell, Mercedes



6) Liam Lawson, Red Bull



7) Franco Colapinto, Alpine



8) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



9) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



10) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi

'We were too quick, that's all it was' - How luckless Norris' speed led to his misfortune

Before the VSC was initiated on lap 14, Norris appeared to be shaping up for a repeat of his dominant recent wins at the Hungaroring and Zandvoort as he raced into a lead of six seconds over Mercedes' Antonelli.

The reigning world champion had come under attack from the championship leader at the race start but Antonelli was soon on the back foot when he cut the first chicane under braking. It put the Italian into the lead on the exit, but he clearly had to give the place back to Norris, which he swiftly did.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli found himself going wide twice on the opening lap of the Spanish Grand Prix

Antonelli attempted to go around the outside of the McLaren again into the next chicane at turns five-six but had to bail out of it once more, again cutting across the run-off. But when he let Norris through for a second time, he was unable to prevent Verstappen following through too at turn seven and so dropped to third.

But Antonelli was soon back ahead of Verstappen after Red Bull told their driver to drop back both behind the Italian and Hamilton having jumped the latter back at turn one by running off track. Verstappen disputed that interpretation of events over team radio, saying he had no choice but to run wide, but heeded the order.

Norris, meanwhile, had quickly set about building a lead and was already 3.2 ahead of Antonelli when Verstappen dropped back on lap four.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris admits team 'were too quick' after missing a crucial VSC pit stop that cost him race lead

The Briton was five seconds clear by lap nine and his lead had grown the lead by a further second by the time the VSC was initiated. In the end, that supreme speed proved to be Norris' undoing, as he was already beyond the pit entry so could not pit immediately whereas his fortunate pursuers were not and so could.

Speaking on team radio after the race, Norris said: "Just take it on the chin. We were too quick, that's all. Very unlucky today guys, we should have won."

McLaren chief executive Zak Brown concurred, telling Sky Sports F1: "That was our race by 20 or 25 seconds.

"He was dominant, he was gone. Managing, great tyre wear - a league of his own."

Is there now any stopping Antonelli in the title chase?

With Norris returning to the track after his delayed and then slow stop initially behind Russell in fifth place before the Mercedes pitted for a second time, a victory for Antonelli appeared almost inevitable despite there still being 40 laps to go.

However, the Italian did not actually lead the race until the end of lap 48 as Ferrari kept Leclerc out on hard tyres in the hope of their being another Virtual or full Safety Car intervention. There was not.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted it wasn't the way he wanted to win and that Lando Norris deserved the Spanish GP victory

As Leclerc's pace eventually started to drop, Antonelli caught up with the Ferrari but, with passing opportunities severely limited around the Madring lap, the Mercedes had to follow behind. That allowed Verstappen and Norris, easily the fastest car on the track, to close right in on the top two before Leclerc finally pitted.

In the end, once in clear air, Antonelli pulled away from Verstappen by four seconds over the closing laps, with Norris unable to find a way past the Red Bull, for his second win in eight days after his stunning back-to-front triumph on home soil at Monza.

Asked afterwards whether he was now starting to think about the championship, the 20-year-old Antonelli cautioned: "That's exactly what I don't want to do.

"I want to keep pushing race by race, keep delivering and keep enjoying it all the way and try to do my best every race and we will see where we end up at the end of the year."

Sports.title: Rams star Garrett to undergo surgery and miss at least four weeks
Sports.content:
Los Angeles Rams star Myles Garrett will be sidelined for at least the next four weeks after being placed on injured reserve with a knee injury that requires surgery.

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year was limited by the issue during training camp and admitted following Thursday's defeat to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne that it had proven more restrictive than first thought.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero was first to report the news on Sunday as the Rams prepare for an extended period without their marquee addition.

Garrett was traded to the Rams by the Cleveland Browns in the blockbuster deal of the NFL offseason, fresh from breaking the all-time single-season sack record in 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch all of Myles Garrett 23 sacks as he breaks the record for sacks in a season for the Cleveland Browns

His arrival was followed by the shock return of Aaron Donald, who stunned the league by coming out of retirement to team up with Garrett at the forefront of the Rams' defense.

Donald was absent in Melbourne in Week One as he works his way back into full football shape.

Garrett is due to miss games against the New York Giants, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Buffalo Bills over the next four weeks. The earliest Garrett would be eligible to return is against the Arizona Cardinals in Week Six.

His introduction in Los Angeles had seen Sean McVay's side, already led by MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford, enter the season widely considered as Super Bowl favourites.

Sports.title: Brighton hit FIVE to leave Coventry without point or goal
Sports.content:
Coventry remain pointless on their Premier League return as they were dismantled 5-0 by brilliant Brighton at the CBS Arena.

Charalampos Kostoulas put the Seagulls in charge before the interval, Malick Yalcouye doubled the lead after the break, and when Taiwo Awonoyi was sent off there was no way back. Pascal Gross' penalty, Lewis Dunk's rocket and Yasin Ayari's strike sealed it.

Brighton had the first seven shots of the match, all inside the first 20 minutes, but Coventry had the next eight and were in the ascendancy - which is what will make Kostoulas' opener more frustrating for Lampard. The Greek striker punished them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brilliant Charalampos Kostoulas finish sees Brighton in front against Coventry

The first half featured 21 shots, the most in any Premier League game so far this season, but Bart Verbruggen kept Coventry out despite the home side having 10 of them. He tipped Jack Rudoni's volley wide and Frank Onyeka's vicious strike over the crossbar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Clinical Malick Yalcouye doubles Brighton lead against Coventry

There was to be no comeback for Lampard's side. The start of the second half put paid to that when Yalcouye nipped in ahead of a sluggish Aurele Florian Amenda to race through and slot home before Taiwo Awoniyi was sent off for elbowing Maxin De Cuyper.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Coventry down to 10 men as Taiwo Awoniyi sent off in the second half

When Bobby Thomas tripped Kostoulas, things got worse for the Sky Blues. Gross converted the penalty to make it three and then Dunk took a pot-shot from distance that arrowed into the top corner of Carl Rushworth's net. Yasin Ayari then made it five in stoppage time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pascal Gross sends Carl Rushworth wrong way to score Brighton's third

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Dunk scores SUBLIME goal of the season contender for Brighton to make it four

Brighton, the Premier League top scorers, go fourth. As for Coventry, their fans were impressively defiant in their support but they remain bottom without a goal let alone a point upon their Premier League return. Hull and Ipswich have started well. They have not.

The key moments from the CBS Arena

27 - SAVE! Verbruggen denies Rudoni from close

32 - SAVE! Onyeka's vicious strike is tipped over

35 - GOAL! Kostoulas strikes to punish Coventry

51 - GOAL! Yalcouye race through to make it two

53 - RED CARD! Awoniyi sent off for a stray elbow

70 - PENALTY SCORED! Gross converts spot-kick

83 - GOAL! Dunk scores with an outrageous effort

90+4 - GOAL! Ayari caps it by curling into the corner

Analysis: Red card was harsh

Sky Sports' Roy Keane on the sending off of Taiwo Awoniyi:

"I think it's tough. Obviously, he's raised his elbow and is waiting for him to come, but is it a swinging elbow?

"I think it's harsh. He probably gave the referee the chance to send him off, but once that decision's made it's proper game over."

Lampard points to missed chances

Coventry boss Frank Lampard speaking in the press conference:

"We went one down from a moment of quality. Welcome to the Premier League, that is what that is.

"The second half, we started again quite well, we had a good chance. Don't take it. The second goal was the most disappointing for us because it's a mistake from our point of view.

"And then the red card changes the face of it a bit, 2-0, 10 men, very difficult. So, lots of circumstances within the game, it feels very difficult obviously to take the result. There are a lot of circumstances that you can reflect on and say, if and if and if.

"We need to just be honest about that, we need to take chances in this league, we need to be efficient in our own box to defend. So, yeah, lots to take from it and not a nice feeling to have that because we haven't had that here for a long time actually."

Dunk's wonder-goal explained

Brighton captain Lewis Dunk speaking to Sky Sports about his goal:

"I've got that sort of shot in my locker, but it was just sitting a bit under my feet, and I thought, just have a shot, and thankfully it went into the top corner.

"I shocked myself. If you see from my celebration, I didn't think I was really going to do it like that, but it was lovely."

Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen telling Sky Sports about the hit:

"I don't think for us it's a surprise, but everyone was really happy to see it come out in a game.

"It was an unbelievable strike, and as a club, we always do a goal of the season, but they can wrap the award up and we can do the ceremony tomorrow because it isn't getting better than this.

"To be fair, he's hit a couple of nice ones in training, but that was very good!"

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler speaking in the press conference:

"Of course it's a special technique, you have to hit the ball in a special place, then it gets a special spin, a special curve, and I think he showed it, it was the perfect shot in that moment.

"But overall, for me it stood out that we kept a clean sheet, he was organising a lot, he was speaking, communicating, he was there when the long balls were coming, so that's for me the most important, and in Germany there's a phrase, the goal was the cherry on the cake."

Analysis: Coventry have support but not quality

Sky Sports' Adam Bate at CBS Arena:

It was quite the sound and the sight, Coventry's supporters singing 'Sky Blue Army' incessantly during the closing stages of their 5-0 defeat. Beaten but not broken by what was a chastening loss by any measure. "Welcome to the Premier League," said Lampard.

Even the delighted Brighton fans, and the final whistle itself, were drowned out in those moments. The Coventry boss applauded the fans. Speaking in the press conference afterwards, Lampard acknowledged the astonishing support from the home crowd.

"There is an understanding, and I'm not asking for sympathy, that the level has gone up. They saw us with 10 men for a long period, I'm not taking that like I'm not grateful, I appreciate very much because it's a help to the players to get that feeling."

Nevertheless, the fear is that it was quality lacking, not confidence.

"The reality, obviously as the boys are finding out, is that maybe there's a millisecond less to get your shot away and there's a bit more pressure in the Premier League," Lampard explained.

"And those things are difficult to just get better." Coventry had many openings far clearer than the ones that accounted for at least

That’s a mighty victory for City, who made light of Phil Foden’s early red card to give United a bit of a lesson in composure, authority and patience. Erling Haaland’s winning goal will be debated to within an inch of its life, but that shouldn’t obscure how well City played – or how underwhelming United were for most of the match. Mbeumo could have done better – he should have driven it low rather than high – but Donnarumma’s reactions were outrageous. Share

Sports.title: Lewis Dunk’s showstopper helps five-star Brighton to rout 10-man Coventry
Sports.content:
The bare facts are bleak: Coventry City are only the second team in Premier League history to lose their first four games of the season ­without scoring a goal. “And yet …” will be the enduring message from Frank ­Lampard to his players.

And yet they have caused prob­lems for opposition teams. And yet they have already faced three of the top flight’s European contingent. And yet they are not altogether playing that badly – the Brighton goalkeeper Bart ­Verbruggen being named player of the match can attest to that. But Coventry des­perately need a point, or even a goal, to give their ­confidence a much-needed boost. It does not take long for a promoted club’s relegation fears to turn to reality.

Goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouyé, Lewis Dunk – especially – and Yasin Ayari were all moments of individual brilliance. But there was also a sense of Coventry self-destruction, with no complaints from Lampard over Taiwo Awoniyi’s red card for an elbow into Maxim De Cuyper’s face, nor the penalty conceded by Bobby Thomas for Pascal Gross to score the ­visitors’ third. There are also legitimate questions to be asked of Lampard’s decision to maintain an attacking approach even after the sending off.

“It’s a difficult scoreline and it’s not easy at home,” Lampard said. “The first half was pretty good, we created some chances, better chances and we had them under a lot of pressure. Then a mistake to make it 2-0 and the red card makes it very difficult.

“It feels very difficult to take the result, but a lot of circumstances that you can reflect on and say: ‘If, and if, and if.’ We need to be honest about that – we need to take chances in this league. It’s not a nice feeling.”

The scoreline certainly lent weight to Fabian Hürzeler’s insistence that Brighton have no attacking concerns despite Danny Welbeck’s summer departure. Brighton have scored more goals and created more big chances than any other club in the Premier League this season – indeed, they have never started a top‑flight campaign with more goals.

“It’s not about having one good goalscorer,” Hürzeler said. “It’s about the flexibility of having many goalscorers and a lot of players who have this desire to score. We were very efficient today and quite ruthless at the right moments in front of goal.”

That was certainly true, beginning with a moment of mastery from ­Kostoulas to break the deadlock, when the Greek teenager showed great poise to control an aerial ball with his foot, nod it between two defenders and then fire into the bottom corner.

That Brighton were not already behind by then was thanks to ­Verbruggen, who produced two excellent saves to deny Jack Rudoni, when palming a volley and a header to safety.

Lampard publicly urged his ­players to “have belief” during the half‑time interval, but then followed two ­minutes that instantly extinguished Coventry’s hopes.

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard endures another glum day in the Premier League with Coventry. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

First came Brighton’s second goal, when Yalcouyé was played in behind the Coventry defence, and the Ivorian’s pace kept all at bay before calmly slotting past Carl Rushworth.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Moments later, the hosts were reduced to 10 men. At first glance, contact appeared accidental between Awoniyi and De Cuyper. But, to the refe­ree Tony Harrington’s credit, he spotted the Nigerian had led with his elbow, prompting a straight red card. To compound matters, the stadium announcer chose that period to tell fans that train cancellations meant there would be no departures from the stadium for 90 minutes after the final whistle.

Thomas’s challenge to bring down Kostoulas inside his own box was as clear a penalty as will be awarded all season and Gross duly stuck the spotkick into the bottom corner.

By the time Dunk sealed the rout with the finest strike of his career – smashed into the top corner from 35 yards – the mass exodus had already begun. It was an outrageous hit, with Dunk saying: “I shocked myself, but it was lovely.”

That was followed in injury time by another excellent finish, this time from Ayari, curled from range into the ­bottom corner.

The only other team to lose their first four Premier League games without scoring were Crystal Palace in 2017‑18. Palace finished 11th that season, but need to pull the emergency Roy Hodgson cord. ­Coventry will hope he is not required here.

Sports.title: Lauren James revels in free role as Chelsea show ‘respect’ by scoring five past Manchester United
Sports.content:
A swaggering Chelsea cast off any suggestion that they had lost the ability to kill off games, putting five goals past a worryingly lacklustre and lackadaisical Manchester United.

Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea manager, said: “When you have the opportunity to really hurt a team, the best way to respect them is to score as many goals as you can, to create as many opportunities as you can.

“Of course, it’s never easy to see the other team or the other manager concede five goals because if I was the other team, I would be really sad. For me, showing respect to the opponent is having that desire and mentality to score as many goals as possible. That’s the difference between the great teams and the good teams.”

United’s players and fans may have preferred disrespect if that is the case. Instead, it was another bruising result for the new manager, Eva Olid, and her side after an underwhelming performance in their 2-1 defeat against London City Lionesses in the opening game of the season.

Olid needed a result to give her some breathing room and her team some confidence, having had just three weeks to get used to one another before the start of the season, and this early into a project there has to be some grace.

For their opponents this game had been talked about as something of a must‑win after the Blues were held to a 1-1 draw by Aston Villa on the opening weekend despite dominating that match.

View image in fullscreen Keira Walsh scores Chelsea’s side's second goal from the edge of the box. Photograph: James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images

To some extent the concern over Chelsea’s profligacy did not need to be too deep. They were at their creative best against Villa and were without the injured centre-forwards Melvine Malard and Mayra Ramírez while Aggie Beever-Jones, who led the line against the Midlands side, had not scored in the Women’s Super League since September 2025. The off-target Beever-Jones was relegated to the bench for the trip to United. Instead, Lauren James and Sjoeke Nüsken worked away interchangeably up front.

The visitors were similarly fluid in other areas too, and that flexibility was super effective. Chelsea were unpredictable and James’s free‑to‑roam role put their star talent at the centre of everything.

Lucy Bronze’s marauding forward yielded the opener when she sent a looping ball over the top and Dominique Janssen should have been first to it, but the United defender misread the fall of the ball and a stalking Wieke Kaptein nipped it away from her. The Dutch midfielder squared to Nüsken who fired in from close range.

The second goal, which eluded them against Villa, arrived just over 10 minutes later. A diving header from the new recruit Andrea Medina cleared a cross whipped in from the left but the hard-working Bronze was there to meet it, clipping it into the path of Keira Walsh, who took a step and powered in from the edge of the box.

The hosts’ heads dropped, which left their manager unhappy. “In football we know anything can happen,” Olid said. “You can be losing 2-0 and can end up winning. I don’t like the heads down. Heads up and we have to continue. Everything is about confidence.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A very brief brighter spell for United after the break was snuffed out by the visiting team and James finally got on the scoresheet after the hour, latching on to Walsh’s defence‑splitting pass and shrugging off Janssen before sending a low drive into the net.

Chelsea’s fourth goal rubbed salt in for a very wounded United side. Janssen, under no pressure, failed to respond to an ambitious burst from Kaptein and the Chelsea midfielder pickpocketed the centre-back and slipped the ball wide to the onrushing Ellie Carpenter, whose first effort was kept out by Phallon Tullis‑Joyce but her follow-up found the net.

Bronze then added to United’s misery during the final minute of added time, hammering the ball in after Walsh knocked a corner back into the melee in the six-yard box.

It became a training exercise for Chelsea and the hosts failed in their attempts to limit the damage. Things look as if they will get worse for Olid’s side before they get better, with a trip to the Emirates Stadium to play Arsenal coming up next weekend, but Olid said she will not divert from the style of football she wants the team to commit to playing.

“If you start changing, then you are never going to build what you want to build,” she said. “It’s a process. I know it’s so hard, the process, because this beginning is hard. Nobody wants to lose games, but we have to be faithful to what we want to do, because I think that long term will give us the wins.”

Sports.title: Rangers lay down Old Firm marker to send Celtic packing from Scottish League Cup
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes has endured a much‑scrutinised start to life at Ibrox but the Rangers manager got the old ground bouncing here as his side dominated Celtic in front of an all-blue crowd to decide the first Old Firm encounter of the season.

Against a backdrop of bouncing techno from the tannoy, Rangers fans celebrated three memorable goals in a thumping League Cup win. A brace for the captain, Dan Neil, bookended Kevin Kelsy’s second‑half finish to put Martin O’Neill’s side down with relative ease. It also showcased a nascent identity for McInnes’s side, one defined by unbending physical commitment and lots and lots of sprinting. The quality of the football may have been patchy, but the commitment was enough to get the 51,212 home fans at the top of their voices.

With away fans banned from Old Firm fixtures this season after the pitch invasion that followed a Scottish Cup tie in March, the atmosphere was always likely to be partisan, if perhaps less heated than is customary. Before the match there was a brisk trade on both Graeme Souness flags and boiled sweets. Inside the ground the Union Bears ultras unveiled a tifo showcasing the apparently resonant moment when Rangers’ Ian Ferguson grabbed Celtic’s Mike Galloway by the lapels during a clash in 1993. A deep cut of a banner, it did a good job of setting the tone for what was to follow.

McInnes said: “I’m delighted. The performance we gave today was the one required to overcome a team like Celtic. I thought the game demanded the players’ full attention and I’m delighted they’ve managed to deliver that. We’ve seen the strength of the club today and it does the players no harm to understand what this match means to so many people.”

Rangers went about the match with an intensity that Celtic struggled to equal from the off, some of their players looking distinctly overawed by the occasion. The former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was among them, flapping at two early openings, but he could do nothing about the opening goal when it arrived in the 22nd minute. After a Celtic counter broke down Rangers immediately turned play around with a long ball to the Celtic area where Cameron Carter‑Vickers failed to properly clear. Kelsy picked up the loose ball, slipped it to Neil and the captain, signed on a free transfer from Sunderland in the summer, placed an excellent shot just inside Johnstone’s left‑hand post.

After seizing the advantage, Rangers went on to dominate the second half and a second goal appeared inevitable. It duly arrived when a free-kick from the impressive James Penrice was flicked on by Ryan Naderi to the back post where Kelsy clipped his effort around the keeper and inside the left-hand post.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Kelsy lashes in Rangers’ second goal around the hour. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Neil then took matters into his own hands with a quarter of an hour remaining as he controlled a loose ball on the edge of the Celtic area and wrapped a shot into the top corner to unleash delirium in the Copland Stand. “I haven’t scored many goals in my career, so to come away with a brace is immense,” Neil said.

It was perhaps just as well for O’Neill that his supporters had been denied access to this match. Celtic began with a calmness that suggested confidence. Ultimately it was more likely to have reflected timidity. The Bhoys were unable to get a foot on the ball at all in the second half, and the big-money signing Kasper Høgh looked lost at the tip of the Celtic attack before he was substituted on 65 minutes.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We were well beaten in the end, on the day we were second best,” O’Neill said. “There has to be a realisation how big this game is, it’s still one of the great fixtures in European football if not the world. We’ve got to know that. We have to learn from it. Hopefully it’s a wake‑up call.”

Rangers will play Aberdeen in the semi-finals, but McInnes was still being asked about Rangers’ stuttering start to the season after this match, generating the timeless response: “Why are you pissing on my chips?”

After this result the Rangers manager can at least look forward with optimism and he could be set to unleash the spirit of Ian Ferguson again as early as next weekend when a second Old Firm derby awaits, this time at Celtic Park.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans in Saudi Pro League after Diogo Jota chants
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo said that fans who appeared to ⁠make chants referencing his former teammate Diogo Jota at Rúben Neves during a Saudi ⁠Pro League ⁠match ​should be banned for life from football stadiums.

The chants occurred on Saturday during ⁠a fixture between Al-Taawoun and Neves’s side, Al-Hilal, in Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.

Jota died last year in a car crash in Zamora, ​north-western Spain, along with ‌his brother André ‌Silva. A close friend of Jota, Neves was a ‌pallbearer at his funeral.

Footage filmed from the stands during the match and circulated on social media appeared to show supporters chanting “Jota”. The shouts attracted the attention of Neves, who pointed to his eye and ‌then up to the sky in response. Passing through the mixed zone after the game, ​Neves said: “I hope they don’t go to pray afterwards.”

In response to an Instagram post showing the footage, Ronaldo commented from his personal account. “The league must take ⁠action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” he wrote. “This ​is no longer football, ​and there have to be limits. People ​who behave ‌like this should ​never ​be allowed to enter a stadium again.“

The game finished 6-0 to Al-Hilal, with Neves playing 75 minutes before being substituted.

Reuters has contacted Al-Taawoun and Al-Hilal for comment.

Sports.title: European football: Lamine Yamal keeps Barcelona perfect, Leipzig rout Hamburg
Sports.content:
Barcelona continued their perfect start to the ⁠season with a hard-fought 4-2 La Liga victory over Levante in Valencia ⁠on Sunday.

Levante ⁠found ​themselves two goals down within 19 minutes after swift play from ⁠Barcelona led to goals for Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal. The home side ⁠then rallied, finishing the half with six ​shots to Barcelona’s ‌three.

Just 42 ‌seconds into the second half, Barcelona were awarded ‌a penalty, won and converted by Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old now has three doubles in his past three La Liga matches.

An errant pass from Espart allowed Levante forward Iván Romero ‌to round goalkeeper Joan García and pass the ball into the net ​with 12 minutes to go. With two minutes remaining, Roger Brugue burst through multiple Barcelona challenges to score a second for Levante.

The ⁠home side’s hopes of a draw were definitively ​ended ​by a mazy run ​and finish from Karim Adeyemi ​in the ‌93rd minute.

Barcelona ​are alone ​at the top of the table with five wins from five, three points ahead of Real Madrid.

RB Leipzig bounced back from their Champions League defeat at Como by thumping strugglers Hamburg 5-0 at home in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

Norway winger Antonio Nusa was the best of the bunch for the hosts, scoring one goal and setting up two more, including one for Christopher Nkunku, the French winger’s first since returning to Leipzig in August.

Tidiam Gomis, Willi Orban and Romulo also got on the scoresheet for Leipzig, who climbed to fourth with the victory.

“It’s easy to look into the past too much. You lost two games. It’s difficult, but you have to look forward,” Nusa said.

“Today we had to perform and we did, so I think we had a good balance of not thinking too much of the past, but trying to attack today and I think we did it.”

Hamburg’s third big defeat in their third league match this campaign leaves the six-time German champions in bottom spot in the table.

Later on Sunday in Spain, Getafe host Deportivo A Coruña before Atlético Madrid visit Real Sociedad.

In the big Bundesliga game, unbeaten Bayern Munich travel to promoted Elversberg, who have won their first two matches. In Italy, Napoli host Bologna, while Juventus are at Sassuolo. Paris Saint-Germain – with just two points from their first three games – will try to kickstart their Ligue 1 campaign at Brest.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta says penalty given to Sunderland ‘unacceptable at this level’
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta’s delight at Arsenal’s latest win was tempered by his fury with the referee John Brooks as the champions triumphed 2-0 at Sunderland on Saturday night.

Before Bruno Guimarães gave Arsenal the lead in a tight match that Régis Le Bris’s team were arguably unlucky to lose, David Raya made a brilliant save to deny Enzo Le Fée from the penalty spot. Arteta, however, did not believe that Ezri Konsa had hauled Dan Ballard to the ground, instead blaming the Sunderland man for pulling down his opponent.

“We had to overcome a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” said Arsenal’s manager. “Sunderland can suffocate you and they decided to be really physical and very direct and we also had to overcome a situation that, in my opinion was unacceptable at this level.

“I’m very worried and sad because this can never be a penalty. It’s a judo roll from the opponent. Ezri does nothing. We have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the win and our momentum. I’m really sad. It should never have happened.”

Arteta, who was booked in the first half for persistently stepping out of his technical area, hailed Guimarães’s goal as “beautiful” after watching Bukayo Saka scored a second goal from the penalty spot in stoppage time, when Sunderland’s Reinildo was sent off for a second bookable offence.

Le Bris was left with mixed feelings. “I’m proud and disappointed, these are the two words that are in my mind at the minute,” said Sunderland’s manager. “I’m proud because I think we showed that we are really close to achieving something big against one of the best teams in Europe right now. After the first half we were a bit reserved with the ball I think, but our second half was excellent.

“We got the momentum, created chances and it was a big save from Raya from the penalty. I think it was very good goalkeeping rather than a poor penalty. Raya was absolutely impressive today.

“We stayed in the game and we created other chances but we didn’t score and that was the difference today.
