Sports.title: De Zerbi says Spurs have ‘mental block’ after wait for league win continues
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi says his Tottenham players continue to lack physical fitness and must “unblock” themselves in psychological terms after they drew their latest Premier League blank in a home 0-0 with Everton. It is now four games in the competition since the start of the season without a goal for Spurs; they sit 17th in the table with two points and were booed off by frustrated fans.

De Zerbi gave a number of explanations for Spurs’ slow start, chief among them the injuries that a clutch of players sustained on the long-haul pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. He lamented the impact of the World Cup on the return dates of certain players and mentioned how Sávio and Omar Marmoush had signed late in the transfer window.

De Zerbi talked up a positive opening 30 minutes from his players against Everton but accepted they ran out of steam and that there was a psychological problem.

“There is a word in Italian – sbloccarsi – that literally translates as if we unblock ourselves,” De Zerbi said. “[It is] a mental block because four games, no wins, no goals scored … it is tough for the players. The team is extremely strong, we can score goals and we can win games. And then we have to respect the history of the players in their careers. Forget Dominic Solanke and Marmoush – the other players … they didn’t score many, many goals in their careers and we have to find these goals. I think we can do so with the quality of our play.”

De Zerbi warmed to a familiar theme when he went back to the pre-season tour. “I said we started this season late for many, many reasons; too late,” he said. “Many players at the World Cup, many injuries, many problems in Australia. Micky van de Ven suffered an injury in Australia. Domi Solanke the same. James Maddison the same. Mateus Fernandes suffered an injury in Australia. He lost 15 days and it’s not so quick. Sávio and Marmoush, they came 10 days ago. I started to work with this [whole] group not last Thursday but two Thursdays ago. So, I think we have not the right physical condition yet.

Sports.title: Phil Foden is SENT OFF in Manchester derby: City star is shown a straight red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes - but Roy Keane claims the United captain should have gone instead
Sports.content:
Phil Foden is SENT OFF in Manchester derby: City star is shown a straight red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes - but Roy Keane claims the United captain should have gone instead

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden was sent off in the Manchester derby in stunning fashion after kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

Old Trafford came alive in the first half-hour when Foden tussled with Manchester United's captain, with referee Michael Oliver adjudging that the England midfielder had violently kicked out.

Replays suggested Fernandes had kicked Foden while on the floor, and Foden responded by extending his legs into the stomach of Fernandes, and was given his marching orders.

Former United defender Gary Neville, who was sent off in a derby in 2004, said on Sky Sports: 'Oh dear. Oh dear, Phil Foden. He's not having it, he's hanging around. Bruno Fernandes has a bit of a kick at him while he's on the ground and Foden reacts. He's kicked him in the stomach. He's not going to get away with that.

'You can see why he is annoyed. He thinks Bruno has had a kick at him. But he reacts badly. VAR described it as a kick with both feet into the stomach.'

He would later brand the act 'a petulant little reaction' to being kicked on the floor, and added: 'If you do that on the floor it is measured differently to someone kicking on the floor. I think it is a yellow card for Fernandes.'

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) September 13, 2026

Phil Foden (right) was sent off in the Manchester derby for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes (left)

Foden was given a straight red card as he protested his innocence to referee Michael Oliver

The ruling from VAR was that there was a 'secondary movement' from Foden and it was a 'clear red card'. It's unclear if there was any check on Fernandes' actions.

Foden is from Stockport in Greater Manchester but let his emotions get the better of him on this occasion.

England team-mate Marcus Rashford was among those calling for a red card, while Foden was consoled by the majority of his team-mates as he left the field.

Good friend and striker Erling Haaland, however, didn't see the need to give any love to the midfielder and angrily ordered him off the field.

At half-time, attention turned to the actions of Fernandes, who had kicked Foden while he was on the floor, triggering a response.

Former United captain Roy Keane said on Sky Sports: 'He (Fernandes) goes and tackles him, gives him a little boot on the floor, he does react obviously. The strange thing is... I'm guessing it's classed as violent. To me, Bruno is the one who is violent.

'We see violence in a different way. I don't think that's a red card. Did the player give the referee a chance? Foden is daft, but so is Bruno. If Bruno got sent off we would be saying he is daft. Bruno has to do better there. Foden, I don't think it's a red card.'

Ex-City defender Micah Richards, meanwhile, added: 'Foden didn't react (in pain). If he reacted at the second kick... if Foden starts screaming, the decision is reversed.

An angry Erling Haaland ordered Foden from the field as other team-mates consoled him

Fernandes had seemed to kick out at Foden initially, triggering the response from the star

'As a referee, it looks worse than it is. I don't agree with the reaction from Foden, but Fernandes started it.'

It comes amid a tough run of form for the 26-year-old, who has not scored in 2026 and lost his England spot for the World Cup.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel was also in the crowd at Old Trafford to watch the game.

Foden was once Premier League player of the season, winning the award in the 2023-24 campaign, but he has struggled to produce performances since, and this is his latest setback.

Sports.title: Kimi Antonelli profits from a Lando Norris mess to win a race he never should have done. The Italian looks unbeatable this season and the chances of a world championship fight look finished
Sports.content:
Every time there is a glimmer, a ray of light behind the curtain, Kimi Antonelli closes the shutters, and the chances of a world championship fight breaking out are finished again.

His latest example of this knack came in Madrid, when he won a race he never should have done.

The victim of ill-fortune here was Lando Norris, who finished third, a place back from Max Verstappen. For the Briton was in command of the Spanish Grand Prix at its shiny new venue on the outskirts of the capital, as he transformed a fabulous pole into a lead over the 20-year-old Antonelli of more than six seconds in the course of 15 laps.

Norris's McLaren is seriously fast after upgrades that show his team under the serious technical leadership of the quietly spoken but impressively methodical Andrea Stella understand the demands of this year's new regulations.

And Norris was, therefore, on the scent of his third win in four races, driving more assuredly than Antonelli, who at least twice ran off the track but was holding on in second place. And, then, a stroke of fortune fell Antonelli's way.

This occurred as Lance Stroll's Aston Martin went into the wall, his brakes apparently cooked. A virtual safety car was deployed. By this stage Norris was beyond the pit-lane entrance. Antonelli was not, and was called in. He was afforded the cheap stop as the action was slowed and Stroll's machine cleared.

Kimi Antonelli celebrates on the podium after winning a race he never should have done

A stroke of fortune fell the Italian's way as he strengthened his grip on the championship

Lando Norris had been leading the way before making a mess of a change of rubber

Next lap, lo and behold, Norris was called in for a change of rubber that lasted a yawning 7.0sec. A mess. The world champion came out in fifth place and 13sec back from Antonelli. How fortunes change.

Norris's chances were extinguished in that brief phase of the race, and it is the Italian who is edging by degrees towards the world title at the youngest age ever, even eclipsing the then 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel. And this in only his second season.

Before us, the truths of Formula One are being redrawn. The old verity that experience counts and you must bide your time is being ripped up as never before.

Antonelli has won eight times this campaign, including unforgettably at Monza a week ago in front of his home crowd. He was cheered and rhapsodised, though his success was in a way only compensation for the partisans after Ferrari performed disappointingly.

He has also gained from the affection and favours of his Mercedes team, from boss Toto Wolff down (my assertion, which they deny). Poor George Russell is hardly the chosen one there. But, it has to be admitted, that in all racing teams love is lavished on the faster of every given pair, and that character is the man-child called Kimi. Russell has won just twice in 2026.

Mercedes believe they have found their star, their future, and who can say they are wrong? Antonelli certainly looks unbeatable this season. The arithmetic supports the assertion. His lead over Russell, who finished fifth, is 81 points with nine rounds remaining.

As for Norris? He is 106 points adrift, which leaves him with an uphill task almost as steep as the North Ridge of Everest.

And Lewis Hamilton, who retired six laps in with brake problems, is barely better placed 101 off the summit. Ferrari are too error-prone and Hamilton is not quite as good as he once was – though he is admittedly rejuvenated this season compared to last – and it will be tough for him to scale the eighth world title he wants to leave as his lifetime's mark.

He clashed with Verstappen on the opening lap. Verstappen passed Hamilton and clawed his way into second place. 'He has to give the place back,' implored the Briton.

Verstappen countered: 'He was out of control.'

Red Bull told Verstappen to yield. He has never been known to pull out of an arm wrestle, and he gave his race engineer and pal Gianpiero Lambiase a blast of industrial language. 'Mate, what the f*** are you guys going on about? We would have shunted.'

After the tough talk, he yielded. But, in a boring race, pretty much devoid of overtaking, Verstappen did hand the place back. But soon Hamilton was plummeting down the field with his technical problems.

'I hit the brake, the car started stopping and then the pedal took a step and, all of a sudden, the car didn't decelerate as fast as it would normally,' explained Hamilton.

Charles Leclerc got the other Ferrari home in fourth place, having led for a long period prior to his late stop. Antonelli resumed the lead, coming home 4.3sec ahead of runner-up Verstappen. Norris harried his pal to the line, just 0.7sec back, in taking the final podium place.

The last words here centre on Antonelli. 'Beautiful work, an absolute masterclass,' eulogised Peter Bonnington, his race engineer.

'Bono', once the voice in Hamilton's ear during his glory days, is chivvying his new student all the way to what now seems to be an inevitable title a few months out of his teens.

Sports.title: Furious Man United fans tell club 'the way you treat us is a disgrace': Supporters unveil protest banner ahead of Manchester derby amid huge protests in front of onlooking Sir Jim Ratcliffe at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Manchester United fans have displayed a solitary banner in the Stretford End at Sunday's Old Trafford derby branding the club a 'disgrace'.

The Red Army opted not to have any other flags or banners at the game against Manchester City in protest over 'the recent behaviour of the club'.

Fans group The 1958 staged a demonstration before the game over United's clampdown on ticket touts, which they claim has targeted innocent supporters.

The TRA, who organise and pay for the flags and banners in the Stretford End, issued a statement on Saturday explaining their actions.

It read: 'On Sunday there will be no flag display on the Stretford End. In its place, a single banner will hang above the players' tunnel with a clear message to the owners, directors and decision-making staff at Manchester United: 'The Way You Treat Us is a Disgrace'.

'This isn't a TRA message, it's a message on behalf of every genuine fan group, match-going supporter, supporters' club and fan representative who has either contacted us directly or been negatively impacted by the recent behaviour of the club.

Manchester United fans have displayed a solitary banner in the Stretford End at Sunday's Old Trafford derby branding the club a 'disgrace'

Sir Jim Ratcliffe was watching on amid huge protests from home supporters

Fans group The 1958 staged a demonstration before the game over United's clampdown on ticket touts, which they claim has targeted innocent supporters

The Red Army opted not to have any other flags or banners at the game against Manchester City in protest over 'the recent behaviour of the club'

'It's an honest, heartfelt cry for recognition from the maligned, vilified, and misrepresented beating heart of our football club – the generational match-going supporters.

'Neither is this solely a Manchester United problem, this is a league-wide crisis that should be addressed at every club, regardless of rivalries and history. Without drastic changes, there will be no rivalries in the future vision for football shared by the decision makers.

'Whilst we still advocate for a change in ownership, we believe that there should be a realistic roadmap for any protest if it is to act as a catalyst for change.

'Unless our generational match-going support is given a real voice that is actually listened to, the little that remains of our fan culture will soon be gone forever.

'TRA aren't a protest group, we're an 'atmosphere' group but we've never shied away from making our position clear when we believe not doing so would be to the detriment of the interests of match-going supporters.

'We hope that you'll understand and support our decision and that those of you who are asking for meaningful change and are able to help will stand up and be counted when called upon in the near future.

'Until then, we'll continue to fully back and support the players and manager throughout, starting with the derby on Sunday.'

United revealed the outcome of their ticket tout investigation on Friday, saying that a total of 685 suspicious accounts have been hit with bans for breaching season-ticket rules.

The club claim to have broken up large-scale organised networks involved in touting and denied that innocent fans have been targeted, adding that some examples of unfair treatment of supporters shared on social media are untrue and don't tell the full story.

Sports.title: Gareth Southgate set to launch new podcast starring his old England favourite, no love lost between EFL and Southampton after Spygate - and toilet roll troubles continue at Man United's Leigh Sports Village: INSIDE SPORT
Sports.content:
Gareth Southgate set to launch new podcast starring his old England favourite, no love lost between EFL and Southampton after Spygate - and toilet roll troubles continue at Man United's Leigh Sports Village: INSIDE SPORT

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

In November, Inside Sport noted how reporters covering Manchester United’s women side when they play at the Leigh Sports Village had taken to bringing their own toilet roll to games thanks to a lack of the product at the council-operated facility.

United have long denied claims of a lack of investment in their women’s team but the noise refuses to go away following the departure of head coach Marc Skinner.

On Sunday, it got louder when they made it back-back losses to open the campaign escaping a lop-sided home clash with Chelsea with a 5-0 pasting while, up in the press box, there was again no loo roll.

Spygate tensions rumble on

As they await the Spygate verdict from the FA, there would appear to be no love lost between Southampton and the EFL. Spies inside the boardroom at Birmingham City have told Inside Sport that EFL chief Rick Parry, who was at St Andrews for the Saints' recent Championship clash, did not speak to any of the travelling delegation, preferring instead to spend the duration of his visit with Blues officials.

The apparent snub did not go unnoticed at Southampton, where there remains some upset about how the decision to throw them out of the play-offs unfolded. While the FA’s punishment remains to be seen, any further measures would no doubt add to that feeling, given the Saints have already paid the ultimate penalty.

EFL insiders say that Parry was in a different area of the boardroom and did not spot the Saints party.

EFL chief Rick Parry, who was at St Andrews for the Saints' recent Championship clash, did not speak to any of the travelling delegation, Inside Sport understands

Chakraborty hard to replace for BBC

Federation bosses are closely monitoring the BBC’s next move ahead of the Olympics following the departure of its head of major events and general sport. Ron Chakraborty is departing the broadcaster at the end of the year after more than 28 years.

He leads the Beeb’s Olympics coverage and, as a highly-respected operator, leaves big shoes to fill. ‘Ron is a great guy,’ explained one source, ‘and did a brilliant job on this year’s Winter Games. It will be interesting to see what they do for LA – producing 35 sports is not easy. There’s nothing like it.’

Some have accused the Beeb, under director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski, of showing little regard for television as it searches for a younger audience by pouring resource into digital output.

Insiders say they are confident in their succession plan, believe in the team that delivered both the summer and winter Games, which remains in place, and say additional leadership oversight will be provided. They reject any suggestion that LA coverage will be compromised given the expertise they believe remains at their disposal.

Southgate set to launch new podcast

Gareth Southgate is set to expand his media empire with a new podcast focusing on managers. Insiders say the show is set to be named The Dugout, and is expected to feature broadcaster Mark Chapman and former Everton defender Conor Coady speaking to bosses from across the game.

Southgate, along with long-time business partner Jimmy Worrall have already launched The Football Boardroom, which aims to take listeners inside the corridors of power.

EFL clubs will meet this week in their divisions to discuss key matters. Inside Sport understands that they will be briefed on the latest with regards to financial distribution, as a deal with the Premier League inches closer.

Gareth Southgate is set to expand his media empire with a new podcast focusing on managers

Russini suffers fresh blow after Vrabel scandal

It would appear that Dianna Russini, the reporter at the centre of a huge NFL scandal, has cast her final vote in the sport’s prestigious end of year awards.

Russini, 43, resigned from her role with The Athletic, in the wake of explosive allegations over her relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. She was one of 50 journalists selected to make picks in the Associated Press’s poll, holding the coveted spot since 2022.

Russini and Vrabel, who are both married with children, denied having an affair after shock pictures emerged of them together at an adults-only resort in Arizona.

However, the images, coupled with further shots which appeared to show the pair kissing in a New York City bar in 2020 led some to call on the AP to release ballots from previous polls amid concerns over integrity. They have declined to do so.

Inside Sport asked AP to clarify whether Russini would be voting this year. They stopped short of directly answering the question however, in a quote, seemed to suggest that would not be the case.

A spokesperson said simply: ‘The makeup of AP’s NFL awards voting panel changes regularly as sports reporters change positions and organizations, and this year is no different.’

Sports.title: Real Madrid take over the Spanish Grand Prix: Jude Bellingham is joined by his brother Jobe and Trent Alexander-Arnold... while Jose Mouriunho interview with Sky Sports' Martin Brundle is awkwardly cut short
Sports.content:
Real Madrid take over the Spanish Grand Prix: Jude Bellingham is joined by his brother Jobe and Trent Alexander-Arnold... while Jose Mouriunho interview with Sky Sports' Martin Brundle is awkwardly cut short

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jude Bellingham led a cohort of Real Madrid stars in attending the Spanish Grand Prix in the capital, as he declared his support for Mercedes drivers.

Bellingham was joined by his brother Jobe – whose Borussia Dortmund team won 3-0 on Saturday – as Madrid hosted a Formula One race for the first time since 1981.

The brothers were seen in the McLaren garage ahead of the race, while they also stopped off with their rivals Mercedes.

Bellingham was seen embracing drivers' championship leader Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, with Real Madrid players and drivers exchanging signed shirts.

Fede Valverde, Vinicius Jnr, Rodrygo and Trent Alexander-Arnold were also among the current Real Madrid stars present.

The trip followed Real Madrid earning a 4-1 victory over Rayo Vallecano on Saturday night, with Bellingham among the scorers for Jose Mourinho's side.

Jude Bellingham and his brother Jobe were among the sporting stars present for the Madrid Grand Prix

The Bellingham brothers visited both McLaren and Mercedes garages ahead of the race

Jose Mourinho and Trent Alexander-Arnold were also part of a cohort from Real Madrid to attend the race after they had overcome Rayo Vallecano 4-1 on Saturday

'Good going, a good start to the season for the team, one little slip up but other than that doing pretty good,' Bellingham said when asked by Sky Sports about their start to the season.

On the Grand Prix, Bellingham added: 'I have been with Mercedes and met George and Kimi, they have been telling us about it [F1] and I have to act like I understand.

'To be honest the level those guys are operating at with the strategy and all those things is a different level.

'It is unbelievable, I am used to a PlayStation controller but these guys are whipping out things with 40 buttons.

'Credit to them and with the work they put in, they deserve everything they get.

'The thing I most admire is the poise of them all, it is really impressive.'

In a separate interview, Bellingham revealed that he typically cheers on Mercedes and British drivers during the F1 season.

Real Madrid boss Mourinho was also present having vowed only to be in attendance if his side were victorious on Saturday.

Mourinho was seen in dicussion with Spanish tennis legend Rafael Nadal at the Grand Prix

Real Madrid great Roberto Carlos spoke to Fernando Alonso in the Aston Martin garage

Mourinho's interview with Sky Sports' grid reporter Martin Brundle was abruptly halted in an awkward moment for the broadcaster.

Brundle had seconds left of his customary segment, and had to cut off the interview after just a brief exchange, when the national anthem began playing with the drivers assembled and Mourinho mid-sentence.

Mourinho was earlier collared by another Sky Sports reporter trackside where he was asked about whether Bellingham could one day be considered England's greatest player.

'Very special,' Mourinho replied. 'Not a bit special, very special.'

Mourinho, however, offered no prediction when asked about how his former club Man United and coach Michael Carrick will get on in Sunday's Manchester derby.

'He's doing well Michael, doing well, I'm happy with that,' Mourinho said.

Mourinho was also pictured in conversation with legendary Spanish tennis star Rafael Nadal at the Grand Prix.

Former Real Madrid greats Roberto Carlos and Steve McManaman were also among the sporting icons present.

Sports.title: Michael Vaughan insists England must win trophies to justify hiring another 'big vibe personality' as Kevin Pietersen takes on new role as white-ball coach - and admits what surprised him about his 'risky' appointment
Sports.content:
Michael Vaughan insists England must win trophies to justify hiring another 'big vibe personality' as Kevin Pietersen takes on new role as white-ball coach - and admits what surprised him about his 'risky' appointment

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Vaughan says England must win trophies after appointing another 'vibe' coach - but insists they couldn't have got a better one than Kevin Pietersen.

The timing of Pietersen's arrival as a limited overs mentor - he starts work today - is curious, not least because England have won 17 of their most recent 19 completed Twenty20 internationals, briefly occupying the world's No 1 ranking in July, and have begun turning the ship around in the one-day format too, claiming series wins over Sri Lanka and India this year.

Vaughan says of the link-up of his 2005 Ashes team-mate with England's white-ball coach Brendon McCullum: 'I like it, it's quirky. It's a risk, it has to be a risk because you're not too sure what you're going to get because Kev's not done a great deal of coaching.

'But his knowledge of batting, his knowledge of winning, his knowledge of playing at the right intensity at the right moments, there's no-one been better in my time playing for England. He'll add that.

'The intriguing part for me is how this works in terms of the different personalities in the backroom team. England have gone for a very powerful, famous backroom team.

'There are a few backroom teams that are doing really well around the world that I don't even know, just quietly coaching and going about their business.

Kevin Pietersen has begun his new role as a specialist white-ball coach for England

The timing of Pietersen's arrival as a limited overs mentor - he starts work today - is curious

Pietersen will work alongside white-ball coach Brendon McCullum in the England setup

'But England have gone for this and have done under Rob Key for a while now, he likes the big vibe of personality. They've got to start winning trophies, to justify all these decisions and, let's be honest a huge amount of money spent.'

Pietersen, 46, was sacked by England alongside coach Andy Flower in 2014, after multiple fall-outs as a player. So, given the acrimonious past, is Vaughan surprised to see him donning the three lions tracksuit again?

'No, I'm happy he's back in English cricket because 2014 I always felt that Kev was dealt an iffy hand. Kev brings a lot of things on himself but there are many others who have done equally silly things and have been allowed back into English cricket,' he explains.

'I was actually surprised they've brought him into the white-ball set-up. I thought the Test team would have approached him. The white-ball team over the last year have been doing quite well. T20s, No.1 in the world. 50-over team, back on track.

'I would think that he will be having an influence on the batters in the white-ball team who play Test cricket.'

Vaughan - speaking to promote the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup, the state school competition he hopes to see expand from 1,100 entrants this summer to 2,000 in 2027 - also believes that Ollie Robinson is the bowler Australia will be concerned about facing most in next year's Ashes after his four Test outings this summer yielded 28 wickets at a cost of single figures each.

'It's just so natural for Ollie Robinson. He just runs in and hits that length naturally,' Vaughan suggests.

'I guess we're all sceptical of what it'll look like in the winter when it's a bit hotter (in South Africa) and he gets into his second, third and fourth spells, comes back the next day and bowls with the Kookaburra ball.

'But here in the UK, I wouldn't want to face him. And the Aussies will know next summer they'll have to try and overcome him one of two ways.

'They'll have to have someone who completely nullifies him technically to see him off or you go the risky game which is Travis Head at the top to try and whack him out of his length. I'll be intrigued to see which way they go.

Michael Vaughan believes England must win trophies after appointing another 'big vibe' coach

England prioritising bowling over pitches, says Trescothick Marcus Trescothick says England are more focused on preparing an elite fast bowling pack than sporting pitches ahead of next summer's Ashes. Signing off before the arrival of incoming Test coach Stephen Fleming on Monday, Joe Root's team completed a 3-0 whitewash of Pakistan as a seam attack marshalled by Ollie Robinson - and including the 90 mile per hour speed of Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue - made the Dukes ball talk in bowler-friendly conditions. Few would argue that the surfaces this summer have offered more lateral movement than others of recent vintage, leading to suggestions that Australia should be presented with a similar set in 2027. But interim head coach Trescothick countered: 'Let's not throw it too far ahead. It's done a bit this season. No doubt about it, more than we've seen in previous years. I don't think we're getting anywhere near looking at the Ashes (though) because we've got a really important series in South Africa. 'There's another transition to happen with Stephen coming in and working with Joe and planning how they're going to move things forward from here. So, I think keep it really simple at the moment and just sit back and enjoy what's happened in the last month. 'I'm not judging on conditions. I think as a general rule our bowling attack is coming into a nice place.'

'I like this attack a lot because it's got all the different variables that you need. I think we've got to be a bit wary of bigging them up too much because of what they've bowled against (Pakistan).

'But if they can keep their mentality and fitness and realise the balls they've bowled in this series are going to challenge every batting unit in the world, they will have things covered pretty well.

'If you cover the basics in Test cricket, it just generally gets you into a good position in most games and series.'

England's next Test assignment is against world champions South Africa in their own backyard in December and one of the most pressing planning issues for captain Joe Root to discuss with newly-appointed coach Stephen Fleming when they meet up in person for the first time this week is how the top six accommodates the return of Jacob Bethell from knee surgery.

Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence both made strong cases to remain in England's first-choice XI against Pakistan, but Vaughan believes Emilio Gay should remain at the top of the order.

'Three 50s in his first six games, and some of the conditions have been pretty tough for batting. I don't think he's completely stamped his name in that first Test in South Africa because to do that you need to get hundreds,' Vaughan reflects.

'One hundred would have probably guaranteed that he played the whole winter. He's looked okay. Looked like he can play at this level, so I'd certainly start with him.

'Other permutations (mean) manoeuvring people out of position. So, that means opening the batting with someone who doesn't open, or hasn't done too much opening the batting.

'Emilio Gay is an opening batter, so I would stay with him for a period. On the South Africa tour, we will find out a lot more about him, a lot more about the team because it's going to be more challenging.'

Sports.title: Furious Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans after fans target Ruben Neves with disgraceful Diogo Jota chants during Saudi Pro League match
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has furiously called for Saudi Pro League spectators who shamefully taunted Ruben Neves with chants about his late friend Diogo Jota to be handed lifetime bans. Footage shared on social media showed Neves responding to Al-Taawoun supporters repeatedly chanting Jota's name in the direction of the Portugal and Al-Hilal midfielder on Saturday. Neves appeared to signal to the fans that 'God is watching', as he pointed first to the sky, then to his eyes and finally in their direction. The Portuguese star could be seen repeating the gesture before returning to the game. Portugal captain Ronaldo posted on Instagram on Sunday: 'The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behavior. This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again.' Neves briefly referenced the incident after Al-Hilal recorded a 6-0 victory over Al-Taawoun, as he quickly walked through the mixed zone post-match. 'I hope they don't go to prayer later,' Neves told reporters, appearing to contrast the behaviour of the fans with religious teachings. Cristiano Ronaldo has furiously called for Saudi Pro League spectators who shamefully taunted Ruben Neves with chants about his late friend Diogo Jota to be handed lifetime bans Ruben Neves was targeted by groups of Al-Taawoun supporters who chanted the name of his late team-mate Diogo Jota during a Saudi Pro League match on Saturday Neves appeared to signal to the fans that 'God is watching', as he pointed first to the sky, then to his eyes and finally in their direction Post-match Neves told reporters 'I hope they don't go to prayer later, appearing to contrast the behaviour of the fans with religious teachings Neves had been the best friend of the late Liverpool star Jota, who tragically died at the age of 28 alongside his brother Andre Silva, 25, after a car crash in northern Spain in July 2025. Neves, who played with Jota at Wolves and with Portugal, had been one of the pallbearers at Jota's funeral. The 29-year-old last year revealed he had a new leg tattoo of him hugging his late team-mate in an emotional tribute, while Portugal decided Neves should wear Jota's No21 shirt. Neves has also been a constant figure of support for Jota's widow Rute Cardoso, who had married the star just 11 days before the tragic car accident, which took place while he was driving back to the UK for pre-season training. The chants from Al-Taawoun fans to Jota have been condemned in Saudi Arabia. Waleed Al-Farraj, a prominent Saudi football broadcaster, claimed the chants lacked 'humanity'. 'For you to say 'Messi' to [Cristiano] Ronaldo, this goes within the competition that exists between them, but to chant at Neves, the Al-Hilal player, with the name of his deceased team-mate Jota, this is an improper act,' Al-Farraj said. 'How do you play on people's sorrows in this way? You must have some humanity.' Ronaldo demanded the Saudi Pro League take action and punish the culprits with lifetime bans Jota tragically died at the age of 28 in July last year following a car crash in Spain Neves and Jota were close friends and played alongside each other on 164 occasions Neves last year revealed a tattoo on his leg of him embracing his friend in a touching tribute Saudi Arabian international Saleh Abu Al-Shamat, who plays for Al-Ahli, also labelled the chants as 'wrong and unacceptable' in a social media post. 'I wanted to draw attention to something we all witnessed today. I felt it was my duty - as a Muslim - to share this and raise awareness,' Abu Al-Shamat wrote on Instagram. 'No one is perfect, of course, but regarding the actions of some Al-Taawoun fans during the match against Al-Hilal: this isn't just about our club; it concerns our great religion, Islam. 'No matter how intense the rivalry or the situation, we should never stoop to gloating over the dead, engaging in slander, or attacking people's families or the deceased. 'We live in an Islamic country, and it is our duty to show the world what Islam truly represents—a religion of love, tolerance, and respect. I hope we can leverage the massive attention our league is receiving to project the best possible image of Islam. 'By doing so, we might foster goodwill and help others learn about our faith. That is the message I wanted to convey; I felt a personal obligation, as a Muslim living in this great Islamic nation, to speak out against what is happening—because it is wrong and unacceptable.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
